508	
509	    /// Darkens the canvas outside a rectangle or ellipse and optionally
510	    /// magnifies what is inside it — a stand-in for a freehand
511	    /// callout (§4.3's M3 list).
512	    ///
513	    /// It lives HERE and not in the Shape pane, where spec §4.3 first listed
514	    /// it, because the zoom half can only be drawn by the layer that owns the
515	    /// pixels: a separate darkening shape could dim the frame but could never
516	    /// magnify it. The centre and the box are SOURCE pixels measured from the
517	    /// centre of the cropped rect — the same frame Crop and Corner Radius use
518	    /// — so they are plain px fields rather than percentages, and the centre
519	    /// is allowed outside the layer (the core only asks that x and y be
520	    /// finite): half a spotlight running off the edge of the frame is a
521	    /// legitimate picture.
522	    ///
523	    /// Eight fields is enough that spelling all of them out at every row
524	    /// would bury the one that changes, so the whole-object write the patch
525	    /// needs goes through `edited { … }` — each row sets its one field on a
526	    /// copy of the current value, and the other seven ride along.
527	    func spotlightSection() -> InspectorSection {
528	        let binding = self.binding
529	        let shapes = SpotShape.allCases
530	        func current() -> SpotlightProps { binding.videoProps.spotlight ?? SpotlightProps() }
531	        func on() -> Bool { binding.videoProps.spotlight != nil }
532	        func edited(_ change: (inout SpotlightProps) -> Void) -> [ReelOp] {
533	            var s = current()
534	            change(&s)
535	            return binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(spotlight: .some(s)))
536	        }
537	        return InspectorSection(
538	            id: "video.spotlight", title: "Spotlight",
539	            summary: { on() ? current().shape.displayName.lowercased() : "off" },
540	            reset: { binding.apply("Spotlight", video: VideoPatch(spotlight: .some(nil))) },
541	            defaultExpanded: false,
542	            rows: [
543	                inspectorCheckRow(
544	                    "Spotlight a region", binding, name: "Spotlight",
545	                    read: on,
546	                    ops: { value in
547	                        binding.ops(
548	                            video: VideoPatch(
549	                                spotlight: value ? .some(SpotlightProps()) : .some(nil)))
550	                    },
551	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight != nil } }),
552	                inspectorPopupRow(
553	                    "Shape", binding, name: "Spotlight Shape",
554	                    items: shapes.map { $0.displayName },
555	                    read: { shapes.firstIndex(of: current().shape) ?? 0 },
556	                    ops: { index in
557	                        guard shapes.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
558	                        return edited { $0.shape = shapes[index] }
559	                    },
560	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.shape } },
561	                    enabled: on),
562	                inspectorValueRow(
563	                    "Center X", binding, name: "Spotlight Center", unit: " px", decimals: 0,
564	                    min: -20000, max: 20000, slider: false,
565	                    read: { current().x },
566	                    ops: { v in edited { $0.x = v } },
567	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.x } },
568	                    enabled: on),
569	                inspectorValueRow(
570	                    "Center Y", binding, name: "Spotlight Center", unit: " px", decimals: 0,
571	                    min: -20000, max: 20000, slider: false,
572	                    read: { current().y },
573	                    ops: { v in edited { $0.y = v } },
574	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.y } },
575	                    enabled: on),
576	                // The core takes width and height as strictly greater than
577	                // zero (`above`, not `at_least`): a spotlight with no area is
578	                // a fully dimmed frame with no way back, so the field's floor
579	                // is one pixel rather than nought.
580	                inspectorValueRow(
581	                    "Width", binding, name: "Spotlight Size", unit: " px", decimals: 0, min: 1,
582	                    max: 20000, quick: [240, 480, 720, 960], slider: false,
583	                    read: { current().width },
584	                    ops: { v in edited { $0.width = v } },
585	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.width } },
586	                    enabled: on),
587	                inspectorValueRow(
588	                    "Height", binding, name: "Spotlight Size", unit: " px", decimals: 0, min: 1,
589	                    max: 20000, quick: [135, 270, 405, 540], slider: false,
590	                    read: { current().height },
591	                    ops: { v in edited { $0.height = v } },
592	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.height } },
593	                    enabled: on),
594	                inspectorValueRow(
595	                    "Feather", binding, name: "Spotlight Feather", unit: " px", decimals: 0,
596	                    min: 0, max: 200, quick: [0, 10, 20, 40, 80],
597	                    read: { current().feather },
598	                    ops: { v in edited { $0.feather = v } },
599	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.feather } },
600	                    enabled: on),
601	                inspectorValueRow(
602	                    "Dim", binding, name: "Spotlight Dim", unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0,
603	                    max: 100, quick: [0, 30, 60, 80, 100],
604	                    read: { current().dim * 100 },
605	                    ops: { v in edited { $0.dim = v / 100 } },
606	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.dim } },
607	                    enabled: on),
608	                // 1 is "no zoom" and 2× is the ceiling `SPOT_ZOOM_MAX` puts
609	                // on it: the pixels come from the same decoded frame, and
610	                // past 2× nothing is left but softness.
611	                inspectorValueRow(
612	                    "Zoom", binding, name: "Spotlight Zoom", unit: "×", decimals: 2, min: 1,
613	                    max: 2, quick: [1, 1.2, 1.5, 2],
614	                    read: { current().zoom },
615	                    ops: { v in edited { $0.zoom = v } },
616	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.spotlight?.zoom } },
617	                    enabled: on),
618	            ])
619	    }

3	/// The Clip tab: a pinned block — the selection header, the action lane and
4	/// the sub-tabs (spec §11 CI-5) — over the sections of the ACTIVE sub-tab.
5	///
6	/// **It owns almost no controls.** The rows are the ones the Video, Audio,
7	/// Text and Shape panes have always built, so this pane holds one instance of
8	/// each — never added to any view hierarchy — and uses them purely as section
9	/// factories. That is safe because a pane holds no state of its own: it reads
10	/// and writes through the shared `InspectorBinding` this inspector handed it,
11	/// and the sections it makes are plain `NSView`s that keep working wherever
12	/// they are added. What this file adds is the header, the Timing section, and
13	/// `makeSections()` — the function from the selection's kind and the active
14	/// sub-tab to the ordered list of sections.
15	///
16	/// **Why the sections are the ones that already existed.** The handoff's table
17	/// draws five groups (TRANSFORM · VIDEO · AUDIO · EFFECTS · TIMING) of four or
18	/// five rows each, but the same document says the pane contents move "into
19	/// sections largely as-is" and that the work is "the shell and the
20	/// kind-to-sections function, not the rows". Those two readings disagree, and
21	/// this is the one that loses nothing: today's twenty-odd sections each carry
22	/// their own Reset button and their own evaluated-action note ("Editing action
23	/// 2's end state"), both of which are per-section by construction
24	/// (`InspectorSection`), and folding five of them into one VIDEO group would
25	/// have to throw away four Resets and four notes. So the existing sections
26	/// stay the unit, the Clip tab lists them all, and the section SUMMARY the
27	/// design asks for — plus Transform open and the rest closed — is what keeps
28	/// the panel readable at that length.
29	final class ClipPane: InspectorPaneView {
30	    /// The five factories. Constructed once and kept: their sections capture
31	    /// them (a Reset closure holds `binding`, a button holds `inspector`), and
32	    /// they are cheap — an `NSView` with a stack view nobody ever lays out.
33	    let videoPane: VideoPane
34	    private let audioPane: AudioPane
35	    private let textPane: TextPane
36	    private let shapePane: ShapePane
37	    private let graphicPane: GraphicPane
38	    /// The sub-tab picked by hand, if any. Forgotten by the CONTROLLER when
39	    /// the selection's ids change (`forgetSubTab()`), never here.
40	    private var chosen: ClipSubTab?
41	    /// The sections the selected action keys, opened once per selection (CI-8).
42	    private let reveal = KeyedReveal()
43	    /// The Look section's gallery model (spec §11 GR-7 [b]), kept here rather
44	    /// than in the section so its thumbnails outlive a rebuild.
45	    let lookGallery = LookGallery()
46	    /// The Curves section's channel, selected point and unwritten list (spec
47	    /// §11 GR-12), kept here so they outlive a rebuild; per window, never saved.
48	    let curveState = CurveEditorState()
49	    /// The Background section's held Status (road map creator-jobs CO3, spec §11 CO-30 (d)),
50	    /// kept here so it outlives a rebuild; its ticker refreshes the pane when the state moves.
51	    let cutoutMemo = CutoutStatus.Memo()
52	    /// The Layout section's choices (road map creator-jobs CO7, spec §11 CO-71), per window.
53	    let layoutState = CameraLayoutSectionState()
54	
55	    override init(inspector: InspectorViewController) {
56	        videoPane = VideoPane(inspector: inspector)
57	        audioPane = AudioPane(inspector: inspector)
58	        textPane = TextPane(inspector: inspector)
59	        shapePane = ShapePane(inspector: inspector)
60	        graphicPane = GraphicPane(inspector: inspector)
61	        super.init(inspector: inspector)
62	        cutoutMemo.onChange = { [weak self] in self?.refresh() }
63	    }
64	
65	    @available(*, unavailable)
66	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
67	        fatalError("ClipPane does not support NSCoder")
68	    }

70	    // MARK: - Shape of the panel
71	
72	    /// The four panes' signatures, composed. Each of them knows something this
73	    /// one cannot see — a filter added, a text family changed, a shape kind
74	    /// switched — and a signature that missed any of it would leave the pane
75	    /// refreshed but not rebuilt, which shows up as controls that never
76	    /// appear.
77	    ///
78	    /// The two halves are added on top of them all, because whether the
79	    /// selection has PIXELS and whether it has AUDIO each add or remove a
80	    /// whole group of sections while every clip id stays exactly as it was.
81	    /// The audio half is the one that moves under an edit: `hasAudio` reads
82	    /// `clip.enabled.audio`, so Detach Audio changes it, and so does the
83	    /// agent's `set_enabled` (§6), which no UI control sends. The video half does NOT track that flag —
84	    /// `hasPixels` asks the MEDIA whether it has a video track, not the clip
85	    /// whether its video is on — so what moves it is a relink or a consolidate
86	    /// that puts different media under the clip. Both are cheap to ask and
87	    /// neither is visible in the four panes' own signatures.
88	    override var structureSignature: String {
89	        [
90	            super.structureSignature,
91	            videoPane.structureSignature,
92	            textPane.structureSignature,
93	            shapePane.structureSignature,
94	            graphicPane.structureSignature,
95	            audioPane.structureSignature,
96	            (binding.videoClips.isEmpty ? "-" : "px") + (binding.audioClips.isEmpty ? "-" : "au"),
97	            activeSubTab.rawValue, subTabs.map(\.rawValue).joined(separator: ","),
98	            matteNote == nil ? "-" : "matte",
99	            // Whether every clip has a look adds or removes Look's Amount row.
100	            videoPane.allLooked ? "look" : "-",
101	            // Whether every clip can be cut out adds or removes Background (CO-30 (a)), and
102	            // whether every clip is a picture its Subject row (CO-108).
103	            videoPane.allCutoutable ? (videoPane.allPictures ? "cutout-image" : "cutout") : "-",
104	            // Whether the selection can be put behind a subject adds or removes Behind Subject
105	            // (CO-55).
106	            videoPane.allBehindable ? "behind" : "-",
107	            // Whether every media has a cursor not in the picture adds or removes Cursor (CU-38).
108	            videoPane.allCursored ? "cursor" : "-",
109	            // Hide While Silent and its "Speech from" list (CO-94).
110	            videoPane.allHideable ? "hide:" + HideSilentSources.candidates(
111	                for: binding.clips, in: binding.snapshot).map { "\($0.id)" }.joined(separator: ",")
112	                : "-",
113	            // A LUT look over a Camera Log file adds Look's warning row (GR-16).
114	            videoPane.lutOverCameraLog ? "twice" : "-",
115	            // A LUT look in an HLG project adds Look's other warning row (HD-13).
116	            videoPane.lutInHLG ? "hlg-lut" : "-",
117	            // The LUTs are the Look gallery's Imported tiles (GR-8 [b]).
118	            LookGallery.luts(in: binding.snapshot).map { "\($0.id)=\(LookGallery.lutName($0))" }
119	                .joined(separator: ","),
120	        ].joined(separator: "|")
121	    }

140	    /// The selection's tabs, in display order: Text or Shape first for those
141	    /// kinds, Picture for clips that draw unless an adjustment clip is among

153	        if !binding.audioClips.isEmpty { tabs.append(.sound) }

279	        // A tab that would open as a column of shut headers opens its first
280	        // section with no stored preference instead. `expandByDefault` defers
281	        // to a section the user has closed themselves, so this is a default
282	        // and not an override — and it is offered to each section in TURN
283	        // because an id can be shared (`video.speed`, `clip.timing`), and a
284	        // group closed once elsewhere would otherwise leave the tab shut.
285	        if !sections.contains(where: { $0.isExpanded }) {
286	            for section in sections {
287	                if section.expandByDefault() { break }
288	            }
289	        }
290	        reveal.apply(sections, action: binding.selectedAction?.id, subTab: activeSubTab.rawValue)
291	        return sections
292	    }
293	}

1	import AppKit
2	
3	// MARK: - Tabs
4	
5	/// The five tabs, in strip order: the three of the chrome cleanup — the
6	/// selected CLIP, the project's media, the document itself — the Transcript
7	/// (spec §11 TX-20) and the Assistant (AI-4). The raw value is the strip
8	/// index, so the order is API: the Transcript's arrival moved the Assistant
9	/// from 3 to 4, and every reader goes through `.assistant` or `allCases`.
10	///
11	/// It was six — Video, Audio, Text, Shape, Media, Document — and four of those
12	/// were the same thing viewed four ways: the selected clip. Collapsing them
13	/// took the whole tab-visibility policy with it (a disabled tab, a preferred
14	/// tab, a pin to defeat the preference), because a Clip tab that lists the
15	/// sections the SELECTION actually has is always the right tab for a clip.
16	/// `ClipPane.makeSections()` is where that decision moved to.
17	///
18	/// The four kind tests below — three of them outlived the tabs they were
19	/// written for — are now what decides which sections the Clip tab shows.
20	enum InspectorTab: Int, CaseIterable {
21	    case clip, media, document, transcript, assistant
22	
23	    var title: String {
24	        switch self {
25	        case .clip: return "Clip"
26	        case .media: return "Media"
27	        case .document: return "Document"
28	        case .transcript: return "Transcript"
29	        case .assistant: return "Assistant"
30	        }
31	    }
32	
33	    /// Whether the clip puts pixels on the canvas — and the test that keeps
34	    /// an audio-only clip out of the video sections.
35	    static func hasPixels(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
36	        switch clip.source {
37	        case .text, .shape, .graphic, .nest, .adjustment:
38	            return true
39	        case .media, .still, .image:
40	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip) else { return false }
41	            return media.hasVideo || media.kind == .image
42	        }
43	    }
44	
45	    /// Whether the clip carries live audio: its media has a track AND this
46	    /// half of the clip is enabled (Detach Audio flips that, §6).
47	    ///
48	    /// A nest clip has no media of its own, so the media test cannot answer
49	    /// for it — and "no" would be the wrong answer, because a nest clip's own
50	    /// volume, mute and fades MULTIPLY every voice inside it
51	    /// (`core/src/audio.rs`: turning a nest down turns everything in it
52	    /// down). What it is asked instead is whether it has audio properties at
53	    /// all, which is the core's own answer to the same question: `nest` gives
54	    /// the clip an `AudioProps` exactly when something inside it can make a
55	    /// sound (`edit_nest.rs`) and `set_audio` errors with "clip N has no
56	    /// audio properties" when it did not. Walking the contents here would be
57	    /// a second copy of that rule, free to drift from the one the writes go
58	    /// through.
59	    static func hasAudio(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
60	        guard clip.enabled.audio else { return false }
61	        if case .nest = clip.source { return clip.audio != nil }
62	        guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip) else { return false }
63	        return media.hasAudio
64	    }
65	
66	    /// Whether the clip's rectangle comes from a decoded source — the clips
67	    /// that get Crop, Colour and Corner Radius. Text and shape clips get
68	    /// Transform, Opacity and Shadow only (§4.3).
69	    static func hasSourcePixels(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
70	        switch clip.source {
71	        case .media, .still, .image: return true
72	        case .text, .shape, .graphic, .nest, .adjustment: return false
73	        }
74	    }
75	
76	    /// Whether the clip is an adjustment clip (spec §11 GR-6): it draws
77	    /// nothing of its own and grades what is behind it, so it gets Color and
78	    /// Clip and never Picture.
79	    static func isAdjustment(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Bool {
80	        if case .adjustment = clip.source { return true }
81	        return false
82	    }
83	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror

  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,

  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));

  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and

  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`

  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).

  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`, +`Reverse`, +`Derived`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries

448	            spaceDidPan = true
449	            panning = CanvasPanSession(origin: point, base: panOffset, offset: panOffset)
450	            return
451	        }
452	        let found = hit(at: point)
453	        if clicks < 2, found.yieldsToObscureGrip, let grab = obscureHit(at: point),
454	           beginObscureDrag(grab, at: point) {
455	            overlay.needsDisplay = true
456	            return
457	        }
458	        switch found {
459	        case .empty:
460	            setCropMode(false)
461	            if !flags.contains(.shift) { clearSelection() }
462	
463	        case .body(let id):
464	            selectClip(id, flags: flags)
465	            if clicks >= 2 {
466	                doubleClicked(id)
467	                return
468	            }
469	            if cropMode, primaryBox?.id != id { setCropMode(false) }
470	            beginMove(anchor: id, at: point, flags: flags)
471	
472	        case .handle(let id, let handle):
473	            beginScale(id, handle: handle)
474	
475	        case .rotation(let id):
476	            beginRotate(id, at: point)
477	
478	        case .cropHandle(let id, let handle):
479	            beginCrop(id, handle: handle)
480	
481	        case .endpoint(let id, let endpoint):
482	            beginEndpoint(id, endpoint: endpoint)
483	        }
484	        overlay.needsDisplay = true
485	    }

487	    /// Mouse-dragged. Exactly one session is live; each turns the pointer into
488	    /// its own ops and pushes them as a live edit, so the box on screen is the
489	    /// core's own answer and a refused tick simply leaves the last good frame.
490	    func continueGesture(at point: CGPoint, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
491	        if var session = panning {
492	            session.update(point: point)
493	            panning = session
494	            panOffset = session.offset
495	            layoutCanvas()
496	            overlay.needsDisplay = true
497	            return
498	        }
499	        // ⌘ suppresses snapping while the drag is in flight, not only at the
500	        // press; the candidate list the gesture fetched is kept.
501	        snapper = CanvasSnapper(
502	            xs: snapper.xs, ys: snapper.ys,
503	            threshold: CanvasSnapper.tick(canvasDistance(CanvasSnapper.threshold)),
504	            enabled: snappingEnabled && !flags.contains(.command))
505	        let canvasPoint = viewToCanvas(point)
506	        if var session = moving {
507	            session.update(point: canvasPoint, snapper: snapper)
508	            moving = session
509	            onLiveUpdate?(session.ops(to: gestureTarget))
510	        } else if var session = scaling {
511	            session.update(
512	                point: canvasPoint, aspectFree: flags.contains(.shift),
513	                aboutCentre: flags.contains(.option))
514	            scaling = session
515	            onLiveUpdate?(session.ops(to: gestureTarget))
516	        } else if var session = rotating {
517	            session.update(point: canvasPoint, snapping: flags.contains(.shift))
518	            rotating = session
519	            onLiveUpdate?([session.op(to: gestureTarget)])
520	        } else if var session = cropping {
521	            session.update(point: canvasPoint)
522	            cropping = session
523	            onLiveUpdate?([session.op(to: gestureTarget)])
524	        } else if var session = endpointDrag {
525	            guard let box = box(for: session.clip) else { return }
526	            session.update(unit: box.endpointUnit(canvasPoint))
527	            endpointDrag = session
528	            onLiveUpdate?([session.op])
529	        } else if obscureDrag != nil {
530	            continueObscureDrag(at: canvasPoint, flags: flags)
531	        }
532	        overlay.needsDisplay = true
533	    }

575	    private func beginMove(anchor: UInt32, at point: CGPoint, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
576	        let ids = selection.contains(anchor) ? selection : [anchor]
577	        var bases: [UInt32: CGPoint] = [:]
578	        gestureTarget = editTarget
579	        for id in ids {
580	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id),
581	                  snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked != true
582	            else { continue }

584	            bases[id] = CGPoint(x: props.x, y: props.y)
585	        }
586	        guard !bases.isEmpty, let box = box(for: anchor) else { return }
587	        snapper = makeSnapper(excluding: Set(bases.keys), suppressed: flags.contains(.command))

593	    private func beginScale(_ id: UInt32, handle: CanvasHandle) {
594	        guard let box = box(for: id), let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else { return }
595	        let route = editTarget.forScale(of: clip)
596	        gestureTarget = route
597	        let start = route.start(of: clip, in: project)
598	        let base = start.video
599	        let rect = startRect(of: box, base: base)
600	        let target: CanvasScaleTarget
601	        if let shape = clip.shape, case .shape = clip.source {
602	            target = .box(shape.boxSize)
603	        } else if clip.text != nil, case .text = clip.source {
604	            // An auto-sized text clip has no stored width, so the measured box
605	            // (divided back out of the scale) is the width the drag starts from.
606	            target = .textWidth(
607	                start.text?.width ?? (Double(rect.width) / max(base.scale, 0.001)))
608	        } else {
609	            target = .uniform
610	        }
611	        scaling = CanvasScaleSession(
612	            clip: id, handle: handle, target: target, base: base, startRect: rect,
613	            rotation: base.rotation, scale: base.scale,
614	            boxSize: clip.shape?.boxSize ?? .zero, textWidth: start.text?.width ?? 0)
615	        onLiveBegin?()
616	    }

658	    /// The keys the canvas owns while it holds first responder. Everything
659	    /// else returns false and walks the responder chain to
660	    /// `EditorViewController.keyDown` (the bare-key transport map).
661	    func handleKey(_ event: NSEvent) -> Bool {
662	        let flags = event.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)
663	        guard flags.subtracting(.shift).isEmpty else { return false }
664	        switch event.keyCode {
665	        case 53:  // Esc
666	            if cancelGesture() { return true }
667	            guard cropMode else { return false }
668	            setCropMode(false)
669	            return true
670	        case 36, 76:  // Return, keypad Enter
671	            guard cropMode else { return false }
672	            setCropMode(false)
673	            return true
674	        case 49:  // Space — armed for panning; the tap is settled on key-up.
675	            guard !event.isARepeat else { return true }
676	            spaceHeld = true
677	            spaceDidPan = false
678	            return true
679	        default:
680	            break
681	        }
682	        let step = flags.contains(.shift) ? Self.nudgeStepLarge : Self.nudgeStep
683	        switch event.keyCode {
684	        case 123: return nudge(dx: -step, dy: 0)
685	        case 124: return nudge(dx: step, dy: 0)
686	        case 125: return nudge(dx: 0, dy: step)
687	        case 126: return nudge(dx: 0, dy: -step)
688	        default: return false
689	        }
690	    }

812	    /// second entry finds nothing to do instead of recursing.

816	        textEditor = nil

818	        editor.onCommit = nil
819	        editor.onEscape = nil
820	        editor.onBlur = nil
821	        editor.onChange = nil

3	/// The preview canvas's geometry and its gesture sessions (spec §4.2).
4	///
5	/// Everything here works in CANVAS space — pixels, origin at the canvas's
6	/// top-left, **y growing downward** — which is the space `canvasRect(of:in:
7	/// sourceSize:video:)` and `canvasAnchor(of:in:video:)` in
8	/// `ProjectSnapshot.swift` speak, and the space the frame recipe describes.
9	/// `PreviewCanvasView` owns the one conversion to and from view points
10	/// (`canvasToView` / `viewToCanvas`, mapped through `AVPlayerLayer.videoRect`
11	/// so handles and pixels cannot drift); nothing in this file knows about
12	/// points, zoom or panning.
13	///
14	/// **The pitfall this file exists to avoid:** placement is *not*
15	/// re-derivable. Cropping removes edges in place and rotation happens about
16	/// the *uncropped* centre, so every rectangle comes from `canvasRect` and
17	/// every rotation from `canvasAnchor` — never from a hand-rolled transform.
18	
19	// MARK: - Rotation
20	
21	/// Rotates `vector` by `degrees`. Canvas y grows downward, so a positive
22	/// angle reads CLOCKWISE on screen — the same sense the canvas's hit boxes
23	/// (`CanvasLayerBox`) un-rotate by, which is what keeps overlay hit-testing
24	/// and the compositor's picture the same answer.
25	func canvasRotate(_ vector: CGVector, degrees: Double) -> CGVector {
26	    guard degrees != 0 else { return vector }
27	    let radians = degrees * .pi / 180
28	    let c = cos(radians)
29	    let s = sin(radians)
30	    return CGVector(dx: vector.dx * c - vector.dy * s, dy: vector.dx * s + vector.dy * c)
31	}
32	
33	/// The inverse of `canvasRotate` — a canvas point taken back into the
34	/// layer's own axis-aligned space.
35	func canvasUnrotate(_ vector: CGVector, degrees: Double) -> CGVector {
36	    canvasRotate(vector, degrees: -degrees)
37	}

41	/// One of the eight scale handles of a selection box, named for where it
42	/// sits in the layer's OWN (un-rotated) canvas rect. The canvas is y-down,
43	/// so "top" is the smaller y — exactly what it looks like on screen.
44	enum CanvasHandle: CaseIterable {
45	    case topLeft
46	    case top
47	    case topRight
48	    case right
49	    case bottomRight
50	    case bottom
51	    case bottomLeft
52	    case left

54	    /// Position in the unit square measured from the rect's centre: -1, 0 or
55	    /// +1 on each axis.
56	    var unit: CGPoint {
57	        switch self {
58	        case .topLeft: return CGPoint(x: -1, y: -1)
59	        case .top: return CGPoint(x: 0, y: -1)
60	        case .topRight: return CGPoint(x: 1, y: -1)
61	        case .right: return CGPoint(x: 1, y: 0)
62	        case .bottomRight: return CGPoint(x: 1, y: 1)
63	        case .bottom: return CGPoint(x: 0, y: 1)
64	        case .bottomLeft: return CGPoint(x: -1, y: 1)
65	        case .left: return CGPoint(x: -1, y: 0)
66	        }
67	    }

69	    /// The handle across the box — the point a plain (no-⌥) scale drag pins.
70	    var opposite: CanvasHandle {
71	        switch self {
72	        case .topLeft: return .bottomRight
73	        case .top: return .bottom
74	        case .topRight: return .bottomLeft
75	        case .right: return .left
76	        case .bottomRight: return .topLeft
77	        case .bottom: return .top
78	        case .bottomLeft: return .topRight
79	        case .left: return .right
80	        }
81	    }

83	    /// Corners drive both axes; edge midpoints drive one.

96	    /// the crosshair rather than a cursor that lies about the axis.
97	    var cursor: NSCursor {
98	        if isCorner { return .crosshair }
99	        return drivesX ? .resizeLeftRight : .resizeUpDown
100	    }
101	}
102	
103	/// Which end of a `line` / `arrow` shape a drag grabbed (spec §4.2's
104	/// endpoint handles). Distinct from `TimelineEdge`, which is a *time* edge.
105	enum CanvasEndpoint: Equatable {
106	    case from
107	    case to
108	}
109	
110	/// What is under the pointer on the canvas. Computed once per press by
111	/// `PreviewCanvasView.hit(at:)` and handed to the session that owns that kind
112	/// of drag, so "what did I grab" is decided in one function instead of being
113	/// re-derived by every mouse handler.
114	enum CanvasHit: Equatable {
115	    case handle(UInt32, CanvasHandle)
116	    case rotation(UInt32)
117	    case cropHandle(UInt32, CanvasHandle)
118	    case endpoint(UInt32, CanvasEndpoint)
119	    case body(UInt32)
120	    /// The void, or the canvas with nothing under the pointer.
121	    case empty
122	}
123	
124	// MARK: - A layer's box on the canvas
125	
126	/// One frame-recipe layer paired with the clip it came from and the source
127	/// size the platform measured for it — everything the overlay needs to draw
128	/// a box, hit-test it, or snap to it.
129	///
130	/// The recipe carries EVALUATED properties (actions already applied, §5.4),
131	/// which is what must be drawn; the ops a gesture emits are written against
132	/// the target's props instead (`CanvasEditTarget`: the base, or the selected
133	/// action's end state), never the playhead's interpolated value.
134	struct CanvasLayerBox {
135	    let clip: ClipSnapshot
136	    let canvas: CanvasSnapshot
137	    /// The layer's evaluated video properties (`RecipeLayer.videoProps`).
138	    let video: VideoProps
139	    /// Uncropped source size: media pixels, the shape box, or the measured
140	    /// text layout box (`LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for:)`).
141	    let sourceSize: CGSize
142	    /// A locked track is drawn but never hit (spec §4.2).
143	    let locked: Bool
144	
145	    var id: UInt32 { clip.id }
146	    var rotation: Double { video.rotation }
147	
148	    /// The rotation centre — the centre of the UNCROPPED rectangle. Cropping
149	    /// never moves it, which is exactly why it is its own function.
150	    var anchor: CGPoint { canvasAnchor(of: clip, in: canvas, video: video) }
151	
152	    /// The cropped rectangle, un-rotated: what the compositor draws pixels
153	    /// into, and what the eight handles hang off.
154	    var rect: CGRect {
155	        canvasRect(of: clip, in: canvas, sourceSize: sourceSize, video: video)
156	    }
157	
158	    /// The same rectangle with the crop taken out — the crop-mode ghost, and
159	    /// the box a shape's unit-space endpoints are measured in.
160	    var uncroppedRect: CGRect {
161	        canvasRect(of: clip, in: canvas, sourceSize: sourceSize, video: video.uncropped)
162	    }
163	
164	    /// A point in the layer's axis-aligned space, taken into canvas space.
165	    func rotated(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
166	        let a = anchor
167	        let v = canvasRotate(
168	            CGVector(dx: point.x - a.x, dy: point.y - a.y), degrees: rotation)
169	        return CGPoint(x: a.x + v.dx, y: a.y + v.dy)
170	    }
171	
172	    /// A canvas point taken back into the layer's axis-aligned space, where
173	    /// `rect` and the crop insets live.
174	    func unrotated(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
175	        let a = anchor
176	        let v = canvasUnrotate(
177	            CGVector(dx: point.x - a.x, dy: point.y - a.y), degrees: rotation)
178	        return CGPoint(x: a.x + v.dx, y: a.y + v.dy)
179	    }
180	
181	    /// Hit test in canvas space, rotation included.
182	    func contains(_ point: CGPoint) -> Bool { rect.contains(unrotated(point)) }
183	
184	    /// The cropped rectangle's four corners in canvas space, TL TR BR BL.
185	    var corners: [CGPoint] { corners(of: rect) }
186	
187	    func corners(of box: CGRect) -> [CGPoint] {
188	        [
189	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.minY)),
190	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.minY)),
191	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.maxY)),
192	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.maxY)),
193	        ]
194	    }
195	
196	    /// The axis-aligned bounds of the ROTATED box — what snapping and the
197	    /// visible-extent tests use, so a turned clip still offers sane edges.
198	    var bounds: CGRect {
199	        let points = corners
200	        guard let first = points.first else { return rect }
201	        var minX = first.x, maxX = first.x, minY = first.y, maxY = first.y
202	        for point in points.dropFirst() {
203	            minX = min(minX, point.x)
204	            maxX = max(maxX, point.x)
205	            minY = min(minY, point.y)
206	            maxY = max(maxY, point.y)
207	        }
208	        return CGRect(x: minX, y: minY, width: maxX - minX, height: maxY - minY)
209	    }
210	
211	    func handlePoint(_ handle: CanvasHandle) -> CGPoint { rotated(handle.point(in: rect)) }
212	
213	    func cropHandlePoint(_ handle: CanvasHandle) -> CGPoint { handlePoint(handle) }
214	
215	    /// The rotation grip, `offset` canvas pixels beyond the top edge along
216	    /// the box's own "up".
217	    func rotationHandlePoint(offset: CGFloat) -> CGPoint {
218	        let up = canvasRotate(CGVector(dx: 0, dy: -1), degrees: rotation)
219	        let top = handlePoint(.top)
220	        return CGPoint(x: top.x + up.dx * offset, y: top.y + up.dy * offset)
221	    }
222	
223	    /// A line/arrow endpoint in canvas space. Endpoints are UNIT coordinates
224	    /// in the uncropped box (`ShapeProps.from` / `.to`).
225	    func endpointPoint(_ endpoint: CanvasEndpoint) -> CGPoint? {
226	        guard let shape = clip.shape, shape.kind.isLinear else { return nil }
227	        let unit = endpoint == .from ? shape.fromPoint : shape.toPoint
228	        let box = uncroppedRect
229	        return rotated(
230	            CGPoint(x: box.minX + unit.x * box.width, y: box.minY + unit.y * box.height))
231	    }
232	
233	    /// The inverse: a canvas point as unit coordinates in the uncropped box,
234	    /// clamped to it.
235	    func endpointUnit(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
236	        let box = uncroppedRect
237	        guard box.width > 0, box.height > 0 else { return .zero }
238	        let local = unrotated(point)
239	        return CGPoint(
240	            x: min(max((local.x - box.minX) / box.width, 0), 1),
241	            y: min(max((local.y - box.minY) / box.height, 0), 1))
242	    }
243	
244	    // MARK: The region frame
245	
246	    /// A canvas point as SOURCE pixels measured from the centre of the
247	    /// layer's CROPPED rect — the frame `video.spotlight`, `video.obscure`
248	    /// and `add_zoom_action`'s region all speak (`model_regions.rs`'s
249	    /// `Spotlight`, and `Compositor.metal`'s
250	    /// `centre = cropped * 0.5 + float2(spotX, spotY)`). Spec §5.3 calls it Q.
251	    ///
252	    /// **It reads the EVALUATED props, and that is the opposite of every
253	    /// gesture session in this file.** Move, Scale, Rotate and Crop all
254	    /// capture the target's props at mouse-down (`CanvasEditTarget.start`),
255	    /// because the op merges into them and a clip inside an action must not
256	    /// be baked to its animated value. A region is measured the other way round: the
257	    /// user drags over what is ON SCREEN, and a source-pixel answer is
258	    /// transform-invariant only if the un-transform matches the transform
259	    /// that drew it. `video` here IS the recipe's evaluated state, so a clip
260	    /// already inside an action scaling it 2× yields the region the user
261	    /// drew rather than half of it — and it agrees by construction with
262	    /// `edit_zoom.rs`, which reads the clip evaluated at the action's start.
263	    /// The two readings differ only once a clip has actions, which is
264	    /// exactly when a zoom action is being added to it.
265	    func sourcePoint(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
266	        let local = unrotated(point)
267	        let box = rect
268	        let s = video.scale > 0 ? video.scale : 1
269	        return CGPoint(x: (local.x - box.midX) / s, y: (local.y - box.midY) / s)
270	    }
271	
272	    /// The inverse of `sourcePoint`: a point in the layer's own source-pixel
273	    /// frame, back on the canvas — what draws a stored region where its
274	    /// pixels are.
275	    func canvasPoint(source point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
276	        let box = rect
277	        let s = video.scale > 0 ? video.scale : 1
278	        return rotated(CGPoint(x: box.midX + point.x * s, y: box.midY + point.y * s))
279	    }
280	
281	    /// A rectangle in the source-pixel frame as its four canvas-space
282	    /// corners, TL TR BR BL — `corners(of:)`'s twin, for the one shape that
283	    /// is axis-aligned in the LAYER's axes rather than in the canvas's.
284	    func canvasQuad(ofSource box: CGRect) -> [CGPoint] {
285	        [
286	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.minY)),
287	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.minY)),
288	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.maxY)),
289	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.maxY)),
290	        ]
291	    }
292	
293	    // MARK: Building
294	
295	    /// The boxes of one composed frame, back to front — the recipe's own
296	    /// order, which is the order the compositor draws in and the reverse of
297	    /// the order the canvas hit-tests in.
298	    static func boxes(recipe: FrameRecipe, snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> [CanvasLayerBox] {
299	        recipe.layers.compactMap { layer in
300	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(layer.clip) else { return nil }

700	    /// constructed with so the grip does not jump to the pointer.
701	    static func angle(of point: CGPoint, about anchor: CGPoint) -> Double {
702	        atan2(Double(point.y - anchor.y), Double(point.x - anchor.x))
703	    }
704	}
705	
706	// MARK: - Crop
707	
708	/// Crop mode's handles (spec §4.2): the same eight positions, but each one
709	/// drives a crop inset in SOURCE pixels instead of the layer's size.
710	///
711	/// Cropping never shifts content (§5.3), so this session writes `crop` and
712	/// nothing else — no compensating `x`/`y`, ever.
713	struct CanvasCropSession {
714	    let clip: UInt32
715	    let handle: CanvasHandle
716	    let base: VideoProps
717	    let sourceSize: CGSize
718	    /// The uncropped rectangle at mouse-down, un-rotated, canvas space.
719	    let startRect: CGRect
720	    let rotation: Double
721	
722	    var crop: CropInsets
723	    var didMove = false
724	
725	    /// A crop may never close a rectangle completely; one source pixel is the
726	    /// floor, which is also what the core enforces.
727	    static let minRemaining = 1.0
728	
729	    func op(to target: CanvasEditTarget) -> ReelOp {
730	        target.op(video: VideoPatch(crop: crop), clip: clip)
731	    }
732	
733	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint) {
734	        let centre = CGPoint(x: startRect.midX, y: startRect.midY)
735	        let v = canvasUnrotate(
736	            CGVector(dx: point.x - centre.x, dy: point.y - centre.y), degrees: rotation)
737	        let local = CGPoint(x: centre.x + v.dx, y: centre.y + v.dy)
738	        let scale = base.scale > 0 ? base.scale : 1
739	        // Source pixels from the uncropped rectangle's top-left corner.
740	        let sx = Double(local.x - startRect.minX) / scale
741	        let sy = Double(local.y - startRect.minY) / scale
742	
743	        var l = crop.l
744	        var t = crop.t
745	        var r = crop.r
746	        var b = crop.b
747	        let limit = CanvasCropSession.minRemaining
748	        if handle.unit.x < 0 { l = min(max(sx, 0), max(sourceSize.width - r - limit, 0)) }
749	        if handle.unit.x > 0 {
750	            r = min(max(sourceSize.width - sx, 0), max(sourceSize.width - l - limit, 0))
751	        }
752	        if handle.unit.y < 0 { t = min(max(sy, 0), max(sourceSize.height - b - limit, 0)) }
753	        if handle.unit.y > 0 {
754	            b = min(max(sourceSize.height - sy, 0), max(sourceSize.height - t - limit, 0))
755	        }
756	        crop = CropInsets(
757	            l: canvasRound(l), t: canvasRound(t), r: canvasRound(r), b: canvasRound(b))
758	        didMove = true
759	    }
760	}
761	
762	// MARK: - Shape endpoints
763	
764	/// Dragging a `line` or `arrow` end (spec §4.2). The model stores them as
765	/// unit coordinates in the shape's box, so the box itself never changes.
766	struct CanvasEndpointSession {
767	    let clip: UInt32
768	    let endpoint: CanvasEndpoint
769	    var unit: CGPoint
770	    var didMove = false
771	
772	    var op: ReelOp {
773	        let values = [canvasRound(unit.x), canvasRound(unit.y)]
774	        switch endpoint {
775	        case .from: return .setShape(clips: [clip], patch: ShapePatch(from: values))
776	        case .to: return .setShape(clips: [clip], patch: ShapePatch(to: values))
777	        }
778	    }

159	    /// The ONE path from the document to this pane. `project` is the handle

201	    /// Places the canvas rectangle inside the void and everything that shares
202	    /// its frame. Called from `layout()` and from `EditorViewController`'s
203	    /// `layoutCanvas` (the split views resize this pane without laying it out).
204	    func layoutCanvas() {
205	        let canvas = snapshot.canvas
206	        overlay.frame = bounds
207	        guard canvas.width > 0, canvas.height > 0, bounds.width > 8, bounds.height > 8 else {
208	            return
209	        }
210	        let available = CGRect(
211	            x: Self.margin, y: Self.margin,
212	            width: max(bounds.width - Self.margin * 2, 1),
213	            height: max(
214	                bounds.height - Self.margin * 2 - Self.captionHeight - Self.captionGap, 1))
215	        var scale = zoomScale
216	        if scale <= 0 {
217	            scale = min(
218	                available.width / canvas.size.width, available.height / canvas.size.height)
219	        }
220	        scale = max(scale, 0.01)
221	        let size = CGSize(
222	            width: (canvas.size.width * scale).rounded(),
223	            height: (canvas.size.height * scale).rounded())
224	        clampPan(canvasSize: size, available: available)

304	        let rect = videoRectInView
305	        let scale = canvasScale
306	        return CGPoint(x: rect.minX + point.x * scale, y: rect.minY + point.y * scale)
307	    }
308	
309	    func viewToCanvas(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
310	        let rect = videoRectInView
311	        let scale = canvasScale
312	        guard scale > 0 else { return .zero }
313	        return CGPoint(x: (point.x - rect.minX) / scale, y: (point.y - rect.minY) / scale)
314	    }
315	
316	    func canvasToView(_ rect: CGRect) -> CGRect {
317	        let origin = canvasToView(rect.origin)
318	        let scale = canvasScale
319	        return CGRect(
320	            x: origin.x, y: origin.y, width: rect.width * scale, height: rect.height * scale)
321	    }

323	    /// A distance in view points, as canvas pixels — how the constant-size
324	    /// grab radii and the rotation grip's offset cross the mapping.
325	    func canvasDistance(_ points: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
326	        let scale = canvasScale
327	        return scale > 0 ? points / scale : points
328	    }

335	        if let cached = cachedBoxes { return cached }
336	        let built: [CanvasLayerBox]
337	        if let recipe = project?.recipe(at: playhead) {

352	    // MARK: - Hit testing
353	
354	    /// What is under `point` (view space). Handles win over bodies, and the
355	    /// primary selection's handles win over everything, so a handle sitting on
356	    /// top of another clip still grabs.
357	    func hit(at point: CGPoint) -> CanvasHit {
358	        if let box = primaryBox, !box.locked {
359	            let grab = Self.handleGrab
360	            if cropMode {
361	                for handle in CanvasHandle.allCases
362	                where near(canvasToView(box.cropHandlePoint(handle)), point, grab) {
363	                    return .cropHandle(box.id, handle)
364	                }
365	            } else {
366	                let offset = canvasDistance(Self.rotationOffset)
367	                if near(canvasToView(box.rotationHandlePoint(offset: offset)), point, grab) {
368	                    return .rotation(box.id)
369	                }
370	                for endpoint in [CanvasEndpoint.from, .to] {
371	                    guard let at = box.endpointPoint(endpoint) else { continue }
372	                    if near(canvasToView(at), point, grab) { return .endpoint(box.id, endpoint) }
373	                }
374	                for handle in CanvasHandle.allCases
375	                where near(canvasToView(box.handlePoint(handle)), point, grab) {
376	                    return .handle(box.id, handle)
377	                }
378	            }
379	        }
380	        let canvasPoint = viewToCanvas(point)
381	        // Front to back: the topmost VISIBLE clip wins. Locked tracks are not
382	        // hit (spec §4.2); hidden ones never reach the recipe at all.
383	        if let box = boxes.reversed().first(where: { !$0.locked && $0.contains(canvasPoint) }) {
384	            return .body(box.id)
385	        }
386	        return .empty
387	    }
388	
389	    private func near(_ a: CGPoint, _ b: CGPoint, _ radius: CGFloat) -> Bool {
390	        abs(a.x - b.x) <= radius && abs(a.y - b.y) <= radius
391	    }

395	    private func selectClip(_ id: UInt32, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
396	        var next = selection
397	        if flags.contains(.shift) {
398	            if next.contains(id) { next.remove(id) } else { next.insert(id) }
399	        } else if !next.contains(id) {
400	            next = [id]
401	        }
402	        if next != selection {
403	            selection = next
404	            overlay.needsDisplay = true
405	        }
406	        onSelectionChanged?(next)
407	    }

433	
434	    private func makeSnapper(excluding clips: Set<UInt32>, suppressed: Bool) -> CanvasSnapper {
435	        let lists = CanvasSnapper.candidates(
436	            boxes: boxes, excluding: clips, canvas: snapshot.canvas)
437	        return CanvasSnapper(
438	            xs: lists.xs, ys: lists.ys,
439	            threshold: CanvasSnapper.tick(canvasDistance(CanvasSnapper.threshold)),
440	            enabled: snappingEnabled && !suppressed)
441	    }

443	    /// Mouse-down. Picks the session that owns the hit and starts it; a click
444	    /// that only changes the selection starts none.
445	    func beginGesture(at point: CGPoint, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags, clicks: Int) {
446	        commitTextEditing()
447	        if spaceHeld, canPan {
448	            spaceDidPan = true
449	            panning = CanvasPanSession(origin: point, base: panOffset, offset: panOffset)
450	            return
451	        }
452	        let found = hit(at: point)
453	        if clicks < 2, found.yieldsToObscureGrip, let grab = obscureHit(at: point),
454	           beginObscureDrag(grab, at: point) {
455	            overlay.needsDisplay = true
456	            return
457	        }
458	        switch found {
459	        case .empty:
460	            setCropMode(false)
461	            if !flags.contains(.shift) { clearSelection() }
462	
463	        case .body(let id):
464	            selectClip(id, flags: flags)
465	            if clicks >= 2 {
466	                doubleClicked(id)
467	                return
468	            }
469	            if cropMode, primaryBox?.id != id { setCropMode(false) }
470	            beginMove(anchor: id, at: point, flags: flags)
471	
472	        case .handle(let id, let handle):
473	            beginScale(id, handle: handle)
474	
475	        case .rotation(let id):
476	            beginRotate(id, at: point)
477	
478	        case .cropHandle(let id, let handle):
479	            beginCrop(id, handle: handle)
480	
481	        case .endpoint(let id, let endpoint):
482	            beginEndpoint(id, endpoint: endpoint)
483	        }
484	        overlay.needsDisplay = true
485	    }
486	
487	    /// Mouse-dragged. Exactly one session is live; each turns the pointer into
488	    /// its own ops and pushes them as a live edit, so the box on screen is the
489	    /// core's own answer and a refused tick simply leaves the last good frame.
490	    func continueGesture(at point: CGPoint, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
491	        if var session = panning {
492	            session.update(point: point)
493	            panning = session
494	            panOffset = session.offset
495	            layoutCanvas()
496	            overlay.needsDisplay = true
497	            return
498	        }
499	        // ⌘ suppresses snapping while the drag is in flight, not only at the
500	        // press; the candidate list the gesture fetched is kept.
501	        snapper = CanvasSnapper(
502	            xs: snapper.xs, ys: snapper.ys,
503	            threshold: CanvasSnapper.tick(canvasDistance(CanvasSnapper.threshold)),
504	            enabled: snappingEnabled && !flags.contains(.command))
505	        let canvasPoint = viewToCanvas(point)
506	        if var session = moving {
507	            session.update(point: canvasPoint, snapper: snapper)
508	            moving = session
509	            onLiveUpdate?(session.ops(to: gestureTarget))
510	        } else if var session = scaling {
511	            session.update(
512	                point: canvasPoint, aspectFree: flags.contains(.shift),
513	                aboutCentre: flags.contains(.option))
514	            scaling = session
515	            onLiveUpdate?(session.ops(to: gestureTarget))
516	        } else if var session = rotating {
517	            session.update(point: canvasPoint, snapping: flags.contains(.shift))
518	            rotating = session
519	            onLiveUpdate?([session.op(to: gestureTarget)])
520	        } else if var session = cropping {
521	            session.update(point: canvasPoint)
522	            cropping = session
523	            onLiveUpdate?([session.op(to: gestureTarget)])
524	        } else if var session = endpointDrag {
525	            guard let box = box(for: session.clip) else { return }
526	            session.update(unit: box.endpointUnit(canvasPoint))
527	            endpointDrag = session
528	            onLiveUpdate?([session.op])
529	        } else if obscureDrag != nil {
530	            continueObscureDrag(at: canvasPoint, flags: flags)
531	        }
532	        overlay.needsDisplay = true
533	    }
534	
535	    /// Mouse-up. Closes the live edit as ONE undo step (§7.6); a gesture that
536	    /// changed nothing registers none, because `endLiveEdit` compares handles.
537	    func endGesture(at point: CGPoint, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
538	        if panning != nil {
539	            panning = nil
540	        } else if moving != nil {
541	            moving = nil
542	            onLiveEnd?("Move")
543	        } else if scaling != nil {
544	            scaling = nil
545	            onLiveEnd?("Scale")
546	        } else if rotating != nil {
547	            rotating = nil
548	            onLiveEnd?("Rotate")
549	        } else if cropping != nil {
550	            cropping = nil
551	            onLiveEnd?("Crop")
552	        } else if endpointDrag != nil {
553	            endpointDrag = nil
554	            onLiveEnd?("Move Endpoint")
555	        } else if let session = obscureDrag {
556	            obscureDrag = nil
557	            onLiveEnd?(session.undoName)
558	        }
559	        overlay.needsDisplay = true
560	        window?.invalidateCursorRects(for: overlay)
561	    }

564	    /// enters crop mode (spec §4.2).
565	    private func doubleClicked(_ id: UInt32) {
566	        guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else { return }
567	        if clip.text != nil, case .text = clip.source {
568	            beginTextEditing(id)
569	            return
570	        }
571	        if setCropMode(true) { return }
572	        NSSound.beep()

575	    private func beginMove(anchor: UInt32, at point: CGPoint, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
576	        let ids = selection.contains(anchor) ? selection : [anchor]
577	        var bases: [UInt32: CGPoint] = [:]
578	        gestureTarget = editTarget
579	        for id in ids {
580	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id),
581	                  snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked != true
582	            else { continue }
583	            let props = gestureTarget.start(of: clip, in: project).video
584	            bases[id] = CGPoint(x: props.x, y: props.y)
585	        }
586	        guard !bases.isEmpty, let box = box(for: anchor) else { return }
587	        snapper = makeSnapper(excluding: Set(bases.keys), suppressed: flags.contains(.command))
588	        moving = CanvasMoveSession(
589	            bases: bases, anchor: anchor, anchorBounds: box.bounds, grab: viewToCanvas(point))
590	        onLiveBegin?()
591	    }

593	    private func beginScale(_ id: UInt32, handle: CanvasHandle) {
594	        guard let box = box(for: id), let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else { return }
595	        let route = editTarget.forScale(of: clip)
596	        gestureTarget = route
597	        let start = route.start(of: clip, in: project)
598	        let base = start.video
599	        let rect = startRect(of: box, base: base)
600	        let target: CanvasScaleTarget
601	        if let shape = clip.shape, case .shape = clip.source {
602	            target = .box(shape.boxSize)
603	        } else if clip.text != nil, case .text = clip.source {
604	            // An auto-sized text clip has no stored width, so the measured box
605	            // (divided back out of the scale) is the width the drag starts from.
606	            target = .textWidth(
607	                start.text?.width ?? (Double(rect.width) / max(base.scale, 0.001)))
608	        } else {
609	            target = .uniform
610	        }
611	        scaling = CanvasScaleSession(
612	            clip: id, handle: handle, target: target, base: base, startRect: rect,
613	            rotation: base.rotation, scale: base.scale,
614	            boxSize: clip.shape?.boxSize ?? .zero, textWidth: start.text?.width ?? 0)
615	        onLiveBegin?()
616	    }

618	    private func beginRotate(_ id: UInt32, at point: CGPoint) {
619	        guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else { return }
620	        gestureTarget = editTarget
621	        let base = gestureTarget.start(of: clip, in: project).video
622	        let anchor = canvasAnchor(of: clip, in: snapshot.canvas, video: base)
623	        rotating = CanvasRotateSession(
624	            clip: id, base: base, anchor: anchor,
625	            grabAngle: CanvasRotateSession.angle(of: viewToCanvas(point), about: anchor),
626	            rotation: base.rotation)
627	        onLiveBegin?()
628	    }

630	    private func beginCrop(_ id: UInt32, handle: CanvasHandle) {
631	        guard let box = box(for: id), let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else { return }
632	        gestureTarget = editTarget
633	        let base = gestureTarget.start(of: clip, in: project).video
634	        cropping = CanvasCropSession(
635	            clip: id, handle: handle, base: base, sourceSize: box.sourceSize,
636	            startRect: startRect(of: box, base: base), rotation: base.rotation, crop: base.crop)
637	        onLiveBegin?()
638	    }

640	    private func beginEndpoint(_ id: UInt32, endpoint: CanvasEndpoint) {
641	        guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id), let shape = clip.shape else { return }
642	        endpointDrag = CanvasEndpointSession(
643	            clip: id, endpoint: endpoint,
644	            unit: endpoint == .from ? shape.fromPoint : shape.toPoint)

656	    // MARK: - Keyboard
657	
658	    /// The keys the canvas owns while it holds first responder. Everything
659	    /// else returns false and walks the responder chain to
660	    /// `EditorViewController.keyDown` (the bare-key transport map).
661	    func handleKey(_ event: NSEvent) -> Bool {
662	        let flags = event.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)
663	        guard flags.subtracting(.shift).isEmpty else { return false }
664	        switch event.keyCode {
665	        case 53:  // Esc
666	            if cancelGesture() { return true }
667	            guard cropMode else { return false }
668	            setCropMode(false)
669	            return true
670	        case 36, 76:  // Return, keypad Enter
671	            guard cropMode else { return false }
672	            setCropMode(false)
673	            return true
674	        case 49:  // Space — armed for panning; the tap is settled on key-up.
675	            guard !event.isARepeat else { return true }
676	            spaceHeld = true
677	            spaceDidPan = false
678	            return true
679	        default:
680	            break
681	        }
682	        let step = flags.contains(.shift) ? Self.nudgeStepLarge : Self.nudgeStep
683	        switch event.keyCode {
684	        case 123: return nudge(dx: -step, dy: 0)
685	        case 124: return nudge(dx: step, dy: 0)
686	        case 125: return nudge(dx: 0, dy: step)
687	        case 126: return nudge(dx: 0, dy: -step)
688	        default: return false
689	        }
690	    }
