692	    /// Focus left the canvas with Space still down (the inline text editor
693	    /// taking over, a click in the timeline). Without this the pan stays armed
694	    /// and the next canvas click drags the whole canvas instead of a clip.
695	    func releaseSpace() {
696	        spaceHeld = false
697	        spaceDidPan = false
698	    }
699	
700	    func handleKeyUp(_ event: NSEvent) -> Bool {
701	        guard event.keyCode == 49 else { return false }
702	        spaceHeld = false
703	        // A Space that never panned is the transport's, and the editor never
704	        // saw the key-down because this view swallowed it.
705	        if !spaceDidPan { onSpaceTapped?() }
706	        spaceDidPan = false
707	        return true
708	    }

710	    /// Arrow-key nudge (spec §4.2). One op per clip and one undo step, the
711	    /// same shape a move drag commits.
712	    @discardableResult
713	    func nudge(dx: CGFloat, dy: CGFloat) -> Bool {
714	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
715	        for id in selection.sorted() {
716	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id), snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked != true
717	            else { continue }
718	            let props = editTarget.start(of: clip, in: project).video
719	            ops.append(
720	                editTarget.op(
721	                    video: VideoPatch(
722	                        x: canvasRound(props.x + Double(dx)),
723	                        y: canvasRound(props.y + Double(dy))),
724	                    clip: id))
725	        }
726	        guard !ops.isEmpty else { return false }
727	        onEdit?("Nudge", ops)
728	        return true
729	    }

735	        guard moving != nil || scaling != nil || rotating != nil || cropping != nil
736	            || endpointDrag != nil || obscureDrag != nil
737	        else { return false }

740	        rotating = nil

754	            let direction = pinchAccumulator > 0 ? 1 : -1

768	
769	    /// An `NSTextView` positioned in canvas space over the text clip. It is
770	    /// axis-aligned even for a rotated clip: AppKit text editing in a rotated
771	    /// frame fights the input method, and the committed string is the same
772	    /// either way.
773	    func beginTextEditing(_ id: UInt32) {
774	        guard let box = box(for: id), let props = box.clip.text else {
775	            NSSound.beep()
776	            return
777	        }
778	        cancelTextEditing()
779	        setCropMode(false)
780	        let editor = CanvasTextView(frame: .zero)
781	        editor.isRichText = false
782	        editor.drawsBackground = true
783	        editor.backgroundColor = DS.chromeBackground.withAlphaComponent(0.92)
784	        editor.textColor = DS.textStrong
785	        editor.string = props.content
786	        fitTextEditor(editor, to: box)
787	        editor.onChange = { [weak self] in self?.refitTextEditor() }
788	        editor.onCommit = { [weak self] in self?.commitTextEditing() }
789	        editor.onEscape = { [weak self] in self?.escapeTextEditing() }
790	        editor.onBlur = { [weak self] in self?.finishTextEditing(commit: true, focus: false) }
791	        addSubview(editor, positioned: .above, relativeTo: overlay)
792	        textEditor = editor
793	        editingClip = id
794	        window?.makeFirstResponder(editor)
795	        editor.selectAll(nil)
796	        overlay.needsDisplay = true
797	    }

799	    /// Commits the edited string as one `set_text`. An unchanged string is an
800	    /// identity edit and the core refuses it, so nothing is sent for it.
801	    func commitTextEditing() {
802	        finishTextEditing(commit: true, focus: true)
803	    }
804	
805	    func cancelTextEditing() {
806	        finishTextEditing(commit: false, focus: true)
807	    }
808	
809	    /// **Pitfall:** tearing the editor down makes it resign first responder,
810	    /// which is the very thing that calls back in here. The callbacks are
811	    /// cleared and the state is nil'd BEFORE the view is removed, so the
812	    /// second entry finds nothing to do instead of recursing.
813	    private func finishTextEditing(commit: Bool, focus: Bool) {
814	        guard let editor = textEditor, let id = editingClip else { return }
815	        let value = editor.string
816	        textEditor = nil
817	        editingClip = nil
818	        editor.onCommit = nil
819	        editor.onEscape = nil
820	        editor.onBlur = nil
821	        editor.onChange = nil
822	        editor.removeFromSuperview()
823	        // Back to the overlay: it holds the canvas keys, and leaving the
824	        // window itself as first responder silently drops every one of them.
825	        if focus { window?.makeFirstResponder(overlay) }
826	        overlay.needsDisplay = true
827	        guard commit, let op = Self.textCommitOp(clip: id, value: value, in: snapshot) else { return }
828	        onEdit?("Edit Text", [op])
829	    }

833	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
834	        DS.canvasVoid.setFill()
835	        bounds.fill()
836	        guard canvasFrame.width > 2 else { return }
837	        // A hairline so a black canvas on a dark void still has an edge.
838	        DS.border.setStroke()
839	        let border = NSBezierPath(rect: canvasFrame.insetBy(dx: -0.5, dy: -0.5))
840	        border.lineWidth = 1
841	        border.stroke()
842	    }

844	    /// The overlay's whole drawing pass. Called by `CanvasOverlayView.draw`,
845	    /// which owns nothing but the event forwarding.
846	    func drawOverlay(in dirtyRect: CGRect) {
847	        guard canvasFrame.width > 2, canvasScale > 0 else { return }
848	        if cropMode, let box = primaryBox { drawCropGhost(box) }
849	        for box in boxes where selection.contains(box.id) {
850	            strokeBox(box, emphasised: box.id == primaryBox?.id)
851	        }
852	        drawObscureRegions()
853	        subjects?.draw(on: self)
854	        if let box = primaryBox, !box.locked, editingClip == nil {
855	            if cropMode {
856	                drawHandles(
857	                    CanvasHandle.allCases.map { box.cropHandlePoint($0) }, fill: DS.snapGuide)
858	            } else {
859	                drawRotationGrip(box)
860	                drawHandles(CanvasHandle.allCases.map { box.handlePoint($0) }, fill: .white)
861	                drawEndpoints(box)
862	            }
863	        }
864	        drawSnapGuides()
865	    }

867	    private func strokeBox(_ box: CanvasLayerBox, emphasised: Bool) {
868	        let path = polygon(box.corners)
869	        // A dark backing stroke first: the coral outline has to survive both a
870	        // white frame and a black one.
871	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.4).setStroke()
872	        path.lineWidth = emphasised ? 3 : 2
873	        path.stroke()
874	        DS.playhead.setStroke()
875	        path.lineWidth = emphasised ? 1.5 : 1
876	        path.stroke()
877	    }

3	/// The preview canvas's geometry and its gesture sessions (spec §4.2).
4	///
5	/// Everything here works in CANVAS space — pixels, origin at the canvas's
6	/// top-left, **y growing downward** — which is the space `canvasRect(of:in:
7	/// sourceSize:video:)` and `canvasAnchor(of:in:video:)` in
8	/// `ProjectSnapshot.swift` speak, and the space the frame recipe describes.
9	/// `PreviewCanvasView` owns the one conversion to and from view points
10	/// (`canvasToView` / `viewToCanvas`, mapped through `AVPlayerLayer.videoRect`
11	/// so handles and pixels cannot drift); nothing in this file knows about
12	/// points, zoom or panning.
13	///
14	/// **The pitfall this file exists to avoid:** placement is *not*
15	/// re-derivable. Cropping removes edges in place and rotation happens about
16	/// the *uncropped* centre, so every rectangle comes from `canvasRect` and
17	/// every rotation from `canvasAnchor` — never from a hand-rolled transform.

19	// MARK: - Rotation

21	/// Rotates `vector` by `degrees`. Canvas y grows downward, so a positive
22	/// angle reads CLOCKWISE on screen — the same sense the canvas's hit boxes
23	/// (`CanvasLayerBox`) un-rotate by, which is what keeps overlay hit-testing
24	/// and the compositor's picture the same answer.
25	func canvasRotate(_ vector: CGVector, degrees: Double) -> CGVector {
26	    guard degrees != 0 else { return vector }
27	    let radians = degrees * .pi / 180
28	    let c = cos(radians)
29	    let s = sin(radians)
30	    return CGVector(dx: vector.dx * c - vector.dy * s, dy: vector.dx * s + vector.dy * c)
31	}

33	/// The inverse of `canvasRotate` — a canvas point taken back into the
34	/// layer's own axis-aligned space.
35	func canvasUnrotate(_ vector: CGVector, degrees: Double) -> CGVector {
36	    canvasRotate(vector, degrees: -degrees)
37	}

713	struct CanvasCropSession {
714	    let clip: UInt32
715	    let handle: CanvasHandle
716	    let base: VideoProps
717	    let sourceSize: CGSize
718	    /// The uncropped rectangle at mouse-down, un-rotated, canvas space.
719	    let startRect: CGRect
720	    let rotation: Double

722	    var crop: CropInsets

725	    /// A crop may never close a rectangle completely; one source pixel is the

729	    func op(to target: CanvasEditTarget) -> ReelOp {
730	        target.op(video: VideoPatch(crop: crop), clip: clip)

733	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint) {
734	        let centre = CGPoint(x: startRect.midX, y: startRect.midY)
735	        let v = canvasUnrotate(
736	            CGVector(dx: point.x - centre.x, dy: point.y - centre.y), degrees: rotation)
737	        let local = CGPoint(x: centre.x + v.dx, y: centre.y + v.dy)
738	        let scale = base.scale > 0 ? base.scale : 1
739	        // Source pixels from the uncropped rectangle's top-left corner.
740	        let sx = Double(local.x - startRect.minX) / scale
741	        let sy = Double(local.y - startRect.minY) / scale
742	
743	        var l = crop.l
744	        var t = crop.t
745	        var r = crop.r
746	        var b = crop.b
747	        let limit = CanvasCropSession.minRemaining
748	        if handle.unit.x < 0 { l = min(max(sx, 0), max(sourceSize.width - r - limit, 0)) }
749	        if handle.unit.x > 0 {
750	            r = min(max(sourceSize.width - sx, 0), max(sourceSize.width - l - limit, 0))
751	        }
752	        if handle.unit.y < 0 { t = min(max(sy, 0), max(sourceSize.height - b - limit, 0)) }
753	        if handle.unit.y > 0 {
754	            b = min(max(sourceSize.height - sy, 0), max(sourceSize.height - t - limit, 0))
755	        }
756	        crop = CropInsets(
757	            l: canvasRound(l), t: canvasRound(t), r: canvasRound(r), b: canvasRound(b))
758	        didMove = true
759	    }

330	/// Spec §4.2's canvas snapping: the canvas centre lines, its edges, its
331	/// thirds, and every other visible layer's edges and centres.
332	///
333	/// The candidates are computed here in Swift from the layer rects — the core
334	/// has no idea where anything sits on screen — but the nearest-within-
335	/// threshold *pick* is `ReelSnap.resolve` (i.e. `rc_snap_resolve`), so the
336	/// canvas and the timeline snap by the same rule. That function speaks in
337	/// `Ticks`, so canvas coordinates are rounded to whole pixels on the way in;
338	/// a snap is always to a pixel, which is what the guides promise anyway.
339	struct CanvasSnapper {
340	    /// Grab radius in VIEW points, converted to canvas pixels per zoom.
341	    static let threshold: CGFloat = 8
342	
343	    let xs: [Ticks]
344	    let ys: [Ticks]
345	    /// The radius in canvas pixels at the current zoom.
346	    let threshold: Ticks
347	    /// Folds together the N toggle and the ⌘ suppression, so no session ever
348	    /// looks at modifier flags itself.
349	    let enabled: Bool
350	
351	    /// What a proposed rectangle has to move by to sit on a candidate, plus
352	    /// the guide lines to draw (canvas coordinates, nil when nothing snapped).
353	    struct Result {
354	        var offset = CGVector.zero
355	        var guideX: CGFloat?
356	        var guideY: CGFloat?
357	    }
358	
359	    /// Tries the rectangle's leading edge, centre and trailing edge on each
360	    /// axis and takes the smallest correction of the three.
361	    func resolve(rect: CGRect) -> Result {
362	        var result = Result()
363	        guard enabled else { return result }
364	        if let hit = best(of: [rect.minX, rect.midX, rect.maxX], in: xs) {
365	            result.offset.dx = hit.delta
366	            result.guideX = hit.guide
367	        }
368	        if let hit = best(of: [rect.minY, rect.midY, rect.maxY], in: ys) {
369	            result.offset.dy = hit.delta
370	            result.guideY = hit.guide
371	        }
372	        return result
373	    }

375	    private func best(
376	        of anchors: [CGFloat], in candidates: [Ticks]
377	    ) -> (delta: CGFloat, guide: CGFloat)? {
378	        var winner: (delta: CGFloat, guide: CGFloat)?
379	        for anchor in anchors {
380	            let (resolved, snapped) = ReelSnap.resolve(
381	                candidates, CanvasSnapper.tick(anchor), threshold: threshold)
382	            guard snapped else { continue }
383	            let delta = CGFloat(resolved) - anchor
384	            if let current = winner, abs(current.delta) <= abs(delta) { continue }
385	            winner = (delta, CGFloat(resolved))
386	        }
387	        return winner
388	    }

391	    /// runaway drag cannot trap the conversion.
392	    static func tick(_ value: CGFloat) -> Ticks {
393	        guard value.isFinite else { return 0 }
394	        return Ticks(min(max(value.rounded(), -1e9), 1e9))
395	    }

402	        let width = CGFloat(canvas.width)
403	        let height = CGFloat(canvas.height)
404	        var xs: Set<Ticks> = [
405	            tick(0), tick(width / 3), tick(width / 2), tick(width * 2 / 3), tick(width),
406	        ]
407	        var ys: Set<Ticks> = [
408	            tick(0), tick(height / 3), tick(height / 2), tick(height * 2 / 3), tick(height),
409	        ]
410	        for box in boxes where !excluding.contains(box.id) {
411	            let bounds = box.bounds
412	            xs.formUnion([tick(bounds.minX), tick(bounds.midX), tick(bounds.maxX)])
413	            ys.formUnion([tick(bounds.minY), tick(bounds.midY), tick(bounds.maxY)])
414	        }
415	        return (xs.sorted(), ys.sorted())
416	    }
417	}
418	
419	/// Trims a canvas coordinate to three decimals before it goes into an op.
420	/// Snapping produces whole or half pixels; this only keeps float noise out of
421	/// the project JSON, where it would make two identical edits compare unequal.
422	func canvasRound(_ value: Double) -> Double {
423	    guard value.isFinite else { return 0 }
424	    return (value * 1000).rounded() / 1000
425	}
426	
427	/// A colour as `video.chroma.key`: exactly three components, clamped to 0…1.
428	///
429	/// That key is the ONE colour in the schema the model spells without an alpha
430	/// (`[f64; 3]` in `model.rs`, and `props_check.rs` bounds each channel), so a
431	/// four-component `RGBA` — which is what a colour well hands back, and what
432	/// the comparison in `changedRGBA` needs — has to be cut back to three before
433	/// it can reach `set_video`. A longer array is not a warning there: serde
434	/// answers `invalid length 4, expected an array of length 3` and the whole
435	/// edit fails.
436	func chromaKeyComponents(_ color: RGBA) -> [Double] {
437	    (0..<3).map { index in
438	        let value = index < color.count ? color[index] : 0
439	        return canvasRound(min(max(value, 0), 1))
440	    }
441	}
442	
443	// MARK: - Move
444	
445	/// Dragging inside the box to move the selection (spec §4.2). Every selected
446	/// clip moves by the same canvas-space delta; the anchor clip's rectangle is
447	/// what snapping tests, so the whole selection clicks into place together.
448	///
449	/// The op writes the target's props plus the delta (the base, or the selected
450	/// action's end state — CI-13), never the evaluated position at the playhead.
451	struct CanvasMoveSession {
452	    /// The target's `(x, y)` per clip, captured at mouse-down.
453	    let bases: [UInt32: CGPoint]
454	    let anchor: UInt32
455	    /// The anchor's rotated bounds at mouse-down.
456	    let anchorBounds: CGRect
457	    /// Pointer position at mouse-down, canvas space.
458	    let grab: CGPoint
459	
460	    var delta = CGVector.zero
461	    var guideX: CGFloat?
462	    var guideY: CGFloat?
463	    /// False until the pointer actually leaves the press point — a click that
464	    /// only selects must not register an undo step.
465	    var didMove = false
466	
467	    /// One op per clip, routed by `target`: each keeps its own position, so
468	    /// a multi-clip move cannot collapse the selection onto one point.
469	    func ops(to target: CanvasEditTarget) -> [ReelOp] {
470	        bases.keys.sorted().compactMap { id in
471	            guard let base = bases[id] else { return nil }
472	            return target.op(
473	                video: VideoPatch(
474	                    x: canvasRound(base.x + delta.dx), y: canvasRound(base.y + delta.dy)),
475	                clip: id)
476	        }
477	    }
478	
479	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint, snapper: CanvasSnapper) {
480	        var raw = CGVector(dx: point.x - grab.x, dy: point.y - grab.y)
481	        let proposed = anchorBounds.offsetBy(dx: raw.dx, dy: raw.dy)
482	        let result = snapper.resolve(rect: proposed)
483	        raw.dx += result.offset.dx
484	        raw.dy += result.offset.dy
485	        delta = raw
486	        guideX = result.guideX
487	        guideY = result.guideY
488	        didMove = true
489	    }
490	}
491	
492	// MARK: - Scale
493	
494	/// What a scale drag is allowed to change, which depends on what the model
495	/// stores for that clip (§5.2).
496	///
497	/// **The pitfall:** a clip has ONE uniform `scale` — there is no per-axis
498	/// scale for pixels. So "edges scale one axis" and "⇧ frees the aspect" can
499	/// only be honoured where the model owns a second number: a shape's
500	/// `width`/`height`, or a text clip's wrap `width`. Everywhere else a drag
501	/// stays uniform rather than pretending otherwise.
502	enum CanvasScaleTarget: Equatable {
503	    /// Media, stills, images, nests — `video.scale` only.
504	    case uniform
505	    /// A shape's box, in model units.
506	    case box(CGSize)
507	    /// A text clip's wrap width (nil = auto-sized); the measured width at
508	    /// mouse-down stands in for it.
509	    case textWidth(Double)
510	}
511	
512	/// One clip resized by one of the eight handles (spec §4.2). ⌥ scales about
513	/// the centre; without it the opposite handle is pinned, which means the
514	/// clip's position moves too — hence the `x`/`y` in the patch.
515	struct CanvasScaleSession {
516	    let clip: UInt32
517	    let handle: CanvasHandle
518	    let target: CanvasScaleTarget
519	    /// The target's video props at mouse-down (`CanvasEditTarget.start`).
520	    let base: VideoProps
521	    /// The uncropped rectangle at mouse-down, un-rotated, canvas space. Its
522	    /// centre IS the rotation anchor, which is what makes the position
523	    /// correction below a plain rotation of the centre's displacement.
524	    let startRect: CGRect
525	    let rotation: Double
526	
527	    var scale: Double
528	    var boxSize: CGSize
529	    var textWidth: Double
530	    /// True once a `.textWidth` drag has actually taken the width path. The
531	    /// other six handles of a text clip fall back to a uniform scale, and
532	    /// `ops` must then emit `set_video` rather than `set_text`.
533	    var widthOnly = false
534	    /// Change in the clip's `(x, y)`, canvas space.
535	    var offset = CGVector.zero

1	import AppKit
2	
3	/// The section header: disclosure triangle, title in the micro-label face, the
4	/// current-state summary, and the Reset or Clear button pinned to the trailing
5	/// edge. The buttons are subviews so they eat their own clicks — everything
6	/// else toggles the group.
7	///
8	/// Spec §11 CI-9: a section EDITING an action (`marks.editing`) shows Clear,
9	/// only while the action keys one of its rows; otherwise it shows Reset, only
10	/// while it differs from its default. Both share the one slot, and at most
11	/// one is visible.
12	final class InspectorSectionHeader: NSView {
13	    var onToggle: (() -> Void)?
14	    var isExpanded = true {
15	        didSet { needsDisplay = true }
16	    }
17	    private var title = ""
18	    /// The last summary and marks drawn, so a refresh only redraws when one
19	    /// CHANGED — the panel refreshes on every document change and on every
20	    /// playhead move inside an action.
21	    private var lastSummary: String?
22	    private var marks = SectionMarks.empty
23	    /// Held so the summary can stop short of the VISIBLE one: they share the
24	    /// header's trailing end, and a summary drawn under a button would be
25	    /// unreadable. Clear is always built; Reset only for a section with one.
26	    private weak var resetButton: NSView?
27	    private weak var clearButton: NSView?
28	    /// The hover (#102, spec §11 CI-15 as amended): a second `DS.hoverFill`
29	    /// over the rest band, faded by its alpha, since a band drawn in
30	    /// `draw(_:)` cannot fade. The first subview, so Reset and Clear sit
31	    /// above it; it stops above the rule.
32	    let hoverBand = InspectorHeaderHoverBand()
33	    private(set) var isHovered = false
34	
35	    override init(frame frameRect: NSRect) {
36	        super.init(frame: frameRect)
37	        wantsLayer = true
38	        hoverBand.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
39	        addSubview(hoverBand)
40	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
41	            hoverBand.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: leadingAnchor),
42	            hoverBand.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: trailingAnchor),
43	            hoverBand.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor),
44	            hoverBand.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bottomAnchor, constant: -1),
45	        ])
46	    }
47	
48	    @available(*, unavailable)
49	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
50	        fatalError("InspectorSectionHeader does not support NSCoder")
51	    }
52	
53	    convenience init() {
54	        self.init(frame: .zero)
55	    }
56	
57	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
58	
59	    override var intrinsicContentSize: NSSize {
60	        NSSize(width: NSView.noIntrinsicMetric, height: InspectorMetrics.headerHeight)
61	    }
62	
63	    func configure(title: String, reset: (() -> Void)?, clear: @escaping () -> Void) {
64	        self.title = title
65	        clearButton = install(
66	            OptionButtonControl(title: "Clear", action: clear, enabled: { true }, onEdit: {}))
67	        if let reset {
68	            let button = install(
69	                OptionButtonControl(title: "Reset", action: reset, enabled: { true }, onEdit: {}))
70	            button.toolTip = "Reset this section to its defaults"
71	            resetButton = button
72	        }
73	        showButtons()
74	    }
75	
76	    private func install(_ button: NSView) -> NSView {
77	        button.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
78	        addSubview(button)
79	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
80	            button.trailingAnchor.constraint(
81	                equalTo: trailingAnchor, constant: -InspectorMetrics.inset),
82	            button.centerYAnchor.constraint(equalTo: centerYAnchor),
83	        ])
84	        return button
85	    }
86	
87	    /// CI-9's one slot: Clear while editing an action that keys the section,
88	    /// Reset while not editing and the section differs, else nothing.
89	    private func showButtons() {
90	        let editing = marks.editing
91	        clearButton?.isHidden = editing == nil || marks.keyed == 0
92	        clearButton?.toolTip = editing.map { "Remove this section from action \($0)" }
93	        resetButton?.isHidden = editing != nil || !marks.differs
94	    }
95	
96	    /// The visible button's title — "Clear", "Reset" or nil.
97	    var buttonTitle: String? {
98	        if clearButton?.isHidden == false { return "Clear" }
99	        if resetButton?.isHidden == false { return "Reset" }
100	        return nil
101	    }
102	
103	    /// The summary's ink: the action's when keyed, the body tier
104	    /// (`DS.textMuted`, spec §11 CI-9) when the section differs from its
105	    /// default, else faint.
106	    var summaryInk: NSColor {
107	        marks.keyed > 0 ? DS.action : marks.differs ? DS.textMuted : DS.textFaint
108	    }
109	
110	    /// Takes the summary and the marks; redraws only when either moved.
111	    func refresh(summary: String?, marks: SectionMarks) {
112	        guard summary != lastSummary || marks != self.marks else { return }
113	        lastSummary = summary
114	        self.marks = marks
115	        showButtons()
116	        needsDisplay = true
117	    }
118	
119	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
120	        onToggle?()
121	    }
122	
123	    override func updateTrackingAreas() {
124	        super.updateTrackingAreas()
125	        // Owner-filtered: a tooltip is a tracking area too (app/CLAUDE.md).
126	        for area in trackingAreas where area.owner === self { removeTrackingArea(area) }
127	        addTrackingArea(
128	            NSTrackingArea(
129	                rect: bounds, options: [.mouseEnteredAndExited, .activeInKeyWindow],
130	                owner: self, userInfo: nil))
131	    }
132	
133	    override func mouseEntered(with event: NSEvent) {
134	        setHovered(true)
135	    }
136	
137	    override func mouseExited(with event: NSEvent) {
138	        setHovered(false)
139	    }
140	
141	    /// The state at once, the band's alpha through `DS.animate` — set
142	    /// directly inside it, never through `animator()`, which animates even
143	    /// outside a group and so would ignore Reduce Motion.
144	    private func setHovered(_ hovered: Bool) {
145	        guard hovered != isHovered else { return }
146	        isHovered = hovered
147	        DS.animate(DS.hoverDuration) {
148	            hoverBand.alphaValue = hovered ? 1 : 0
149	        }
150	    }
151	
152	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
153	        // **Pitfall:** `DS.hoverFill` is `quaternaryLabelColor`, which is
154	        // ALREADY about 10% ink — taking 0.35 of it left a 3.5% wash that is
155	        // invisible in the light appearance, so the header did not separate
156	        // from the rows under it. Drawn at its own alpha it is a quiet band
157	        // that reads in both appearances.
158	        DS.hoverFill.setFill()
159	        bounds.fill()
160	        DS.border.setFill()
161	        NSRect(x: 0, y: bounds.height - 1, width: bounds.width, height: 1).fill()
162	
163	        let glyph = isExpanded ? "chevron.down" : "chevron.right"
164	        let box = NSRect(x: InspectorMetrics.inset, y: bounds.midY - 5, width: 10, height: 10)
165	        if let icon = NSImage(systemSymbolName: glyph, accessibilityDescription: title)?
166	            .withSymbolConfiguration(NSImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: 9, weight: .semibold))
167	        {
168	            let tinted = icon.tinted(with: DS.textMuted)
169	            let size = tinted.size
170	            tinted.draw(
171	                in: NSRect(
172	                    x: box.minX, y: box.midY - size.height / 2, width: size.width,
173	                    height: size.height))
174	        } else {
175	            let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
176	                .font: DS.sans(9), .foregroundColor: DS.textMuted,
177	            ]
178	            (isExpanded ? "▾" : "▸").draw(
179	                at: NSPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.minY), withAttributes: attributes)
180	        }
181	
182	        let label = Self.titleLabel(title)
183	        label.draw(at: NSPoint(x: box.maxX + 6, y: bounds.midY - label.size().height / 2))
184	        drawSummary(after: drawMarks(after: box.maxX + 6 + label.size().width))
185	    }
186	
187	    /// `◆N` in the action ink, then ◇ and ⊘ faint, after the title; answers
188	    /// where they end.
189	    private func drawMarks(after titleEnd: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
190	        var x = titleEnd
191	        var parts: [(String, NSFont, NSColor)] = []
192	        if marks.keyed > 0 {
193	            parts.append(("◆\(marks.keyed)", DS.mono(9, weight: .medium), DS.action))
194	        }
195	        if marks.other { parts.append(("◇", DS.mono(9), DS.textFaint)) }
196	        if marks.allNotAnimatable { parts.append(("⊘", DS.mono(9), DS.textFaint)) }
197	        for (text, font, ink) in parts {
198	            let mark = NSAttributedString(
199	                string: text, attributes: [.font: font, .foregroundColor: ink])
200	            let size = mark.size()
201	            mark.draw(at: NSPoint(x: x + 6, y: bounds.midY - size.height / 2))
202	            x += 6 + size.width
203	        }
204	        return x
205	    }
206	
207	    /// The title in the micro-label FACE — mono 10, uppercase, 0.09em tracking
208	    /// — but not in the micro-label's ink.
209	    ///
210	    /// **Pitfall:** `DS.microLabel` paints in `DS.textFaint`
211	    /// (`tertiaryLabelColor`), which over this header's fill is grey on grey;
212	    /// with the Clip tab now stacking up to twenty collapsed headers, that
213	    /// reads as a list of DISABLED rows rather than a list of groups. Built
214	    /// here rather than by changing `DS.microLabel`, whose other callers draw
215	    /// one quiet label over the chrome, where faint is right. The summary
216	    /// beside it stays `textFaint`: it is secondary to the title.
217	    private static func titleLabel(_ title: String) -> NSAttributedString {
218	        let size: CGFloat = 10
219	        return NSAttributedString(
220	            string: title.uppercased(),
221	            attributes: [
222	                .font: DS.mono(size), .kern: size * 0.09, .foregroundColor: DS.textMuted,
223	            ])
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The state summary, right-aligned in whatever room is left between the
227	    /// title and the visible button. Truncated rather than clipped: it is a
228	    /// sentence fragment, and half a word with no ellipsis reads as a bug.
229	    private func drawSummary(after titleEnd: CGFloat) {
230	        guard let text = lastSummary, !text.isEmpty else { return }
231	        // A button that Auto Layout has not placed yet has a zero frame, and
232	        // taking its minX would put the summary's right edge at −6 and skip it
233	        // below. `refresh(summary:marks:)` only redraws when the summary or
234	        // the marks change, so a summary skipped on the first pass would stay
235	        // missing until one moved — hence the unplaced button falls back to
236	        // the inset.
237	        let visible = [clearButton, resetButton].compactMap { $0 }.first { !$0.isHidden }
238	        let button = visible.map { $0.frame.width > 0 ? $0.frame.minX : nil } ?? nil
239	        let right = (button ?? bounds.width - InspectorMetrics.inset) - 6
240	        let left = titleEnd + 8
241	        guard right - left > 14 else { return }
242	        let paragraph = NSMutableParagraphStyle()
243	        paragraph.alignment = .right
244	        paragraph.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
245	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
246	            .font: DS.mono(10), .foregroundColor: summaryInk,
247	            .paragraphStyle: paragraph,
248	        ]
249	        let height = text.size(withAttributes: attributes).height
250	        text.draw(
251	            in: NSRect(x: left, y: bounds.midY - height / 2, width: right - left, height: height),
252	            withAttributes: attributes)
253	    }
254	}
255	
256	/// The section header's hover band: `DS.hoverFill` over the header's own,
257	/// one step darker, shown and hidden by its alpha. Clicks pass through to
258	/// the header.
259	final class InspectorHeaderHoverBand: NSView {
260	    override init(frame frameRect: NSRect) {
261	        super.init(frame: frameRect)
262	        wantsLayer = true
263	        alphaValue = 0
264	    }
265	
266	    @available(*, unavailable)
267	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
268	        fatalError("InspectorHeaderHoverBand does not support NSCoder")
269	    }
270	
271	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
272	
273	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
274	        DS.hoverFill.setFill()
275	        bounds.fill(using: .sourceOver)
276	    }
277	
278	    override func hitTest(_ point: NSPoint) -> NSView? {
279	        nil
280	    }
281	}

1	import AppKit
2	
3	// MARK: - Sections
4	
5	/// One disclosure group: a header with the title, a right-aligned summary of
6	/// what the group currently says, an optional reset-to-default button, and the
7	/// rows. Collapsed state is per section id in `UserDefaults`, so a pane
8	/// rebuilt after every edit does not keep re-opening a group the user closed.
9	///
10	/// **The stored value records COLLAPSED, not expanded** — a section nobody has
11	/// touched has no stored value at all, which is what lets `defaultExpanded`
12	/// mean anything. Flipping that spelling would invert every saved panel.
13	final class InspectorSection: NSView {
14	    /// `UserDefaults` key prefix; the suffix is the section's stable id.
15	    static let collapsedKeyPrefix = "FrameJobInspectorSection."
16	
17	    let id: String
18	    let title: String
19	    let header = InspectorSectionHeader()
20	    private let content = NSStackView()
21	    private(set) var isExpanded = true
22	    private let summary: (() -> String?)?
23	    /// An explicit "differs from its default" (spec §11 CI-9), for a section
24	    /// whose rows do not read the props or whose Reset writes fewer keys
25	    /// than its rows read; nil folds the rows' own defaults.
26	    private let differs: (() -> Bool)?
27	    /// The rows' marks, folded (road map 9 §5) at the end of `init` and on
28	    /// every `refresh()`.
29	    private(set) var marks = SectionMarks.empty
30	    /// "Actions don't animate this" — shown while every row that writes is ⊘.
31	    private var inertNote: InspectorNoteLabel?
32	    /// The header's click, after the preference is stored — and nothing else:
33	    /// `reveal()` and `expandByDefault()` never call it (`KeyedReveal`).
34	    var didToggle: ((InspectorSection) -> Void)?
35	
36	    /// `summary` is a closure rather than a string because it is re-read on
37	    /// every `refresh()`: a collapsed section still has to tell the truth
38	    /// about the value under it. `defaultExpanded` is the state before the
39	    /// user has ever touched THIS section — the design opens Transform and
40	    /// the primary section of a text or shape selection, and closes the rest.
41	    init(
42	        id: String, title: String, summary: (() -> String?)? = nil,
43	        note: (() -> String?)? = nil, reset: (() -> Void)? = nil,
44	        differs: (() -> Bool)? = nil, defaultExpanded: Bool = true, rows: [NSView]
45	    ) {
46	        self.id = id
47	        self.title = title
48	        self.summary = summary
49	        self.differs = differs
50	        super.init(frame: .zero)
51	        let key = Self.collapsedKeyPrefix + id
52	        if let collapsed = UserDefaults.standard.object(forKey: key) as? Bool {
53	            isExpanded = !collapsed
54	        } else {
55	            isExpanded = defaultExpanded
56	        }
57	
58	        content.orientation = .vertical
59	        content.alignment = .leading
60	        content.spacing = InspectorMetrics.rowSpacing
61	        content.edgeInsets = NSEdgeInsets(
62	            top: 2, left: InspectorMetrics.inset, bottom: 8, right: InspectorMetrics.inset)
63	        let inert = InspectorNoteLabel { [weak self] in
64	            self?.marks.allNotAnimatable == true
65	                ? "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." : nil
66	        }
67	        inert.textColor = DS.textFaint
68	        inertNote = inert
69	        addRow(inert)
70	        if let note = note {
71	            addRow(InspectorNoteLabel(note: note))
72	        }
73	        for row in rows { addRow(row) }
74	
75	        header.configure(title: title, reset: reset, clear: { [weak self] in self?.clear() })
76	        header.onToggle = { [weak self] in self?.toggle() }
77	
78	        let stack = NSStackView(views: [header, content])
79	        stack.orientation = .vertical
80	        stack.alignment = .leading
81	        stack.spacing = 0
82	        stack.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
83	        addSubview(stack)
84	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
85	            stack.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor),
86	            stack.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bottomAnchor),
87	            stack.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: leadingAnchor),
88	            stack.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: trailingAnchor),
89	            header.widthAnchor.constraint(equalTo: stack.widthAnchor),
90	            content.widthAnchor.constraint(equalTo: stack.widthAnchor),
91	        ])
92	        content.isHidden = !isExpanded
93	        header.isExpanded = isExpanded
94	        for gutter in Self.gutters(in: content) { gutter.refresh() }
95	        foldMarks()
96	    }
97	
98	    @available(*, unavailable)
99	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
100	        fatalError("InspectorSection does not support NSCoder")
101	    }
102	
103	    private func addRow(_ row: NSView) {
104	        content.addArrangedSubview(row)
105	        row.widthAnchor.constraint(
106	            equalTo: content.widthAnchor, constant: -2 * InspectorMetrics.inset).isActive = true
107	    }
108	
109	    private func toggle() {
110	        isExpanded.toggle()
111	        // The redesign's one animation (spec §11 CI-15): through `DS.animate`,
112	        // which runs it unanimated under Reduce Motion. The state is set at once.
113	        DS.animate(DS.stateDuration) {
114	            content.isHidden = !isExpanded
115	            superview?.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
116	        }
117	        header.isExpanded = isExpanded
118	        UserDefaults.standard.set(!isExpanded, forKey: Self.collapsedKeyPrefix + id)
119	        didToggle?(self)
120	    }

122	    /// Opens the section and writes NO preference — the selected action's
123	    /// auto-open (spec §11 CI-8), which must leave the person's own layout
124	    /// standing for when the action is left.
125	    func reveal() {
126	        isExpanded = true
127	        content.isHidden = false
128	        header.isExpanded = true
129	    }

131	    /// Opens the section as a DEFAULT, for a pane that decided after building
132	    /// it that this is the group to open (`ClipPane`'s "the first section is
133	    /// open when there is no Transform"). `defaultExpanded` cannot say it: the
134	    /// pane only knows which section is first once it has them all.
135	    ///
136	    /// **It defers to the user and writes nothing.** A section the user has
137	    /// ever toggled has a stored value, and re-opening a group somebody closed
138	    /// on every rebuild would be worse than the closed panel this fixes;
139	    /// storing the state here would then make that override permanent.
140	    /// Returns whether it opened the section, so a caller walking a list can
141	    /// stop at the first one that had no stored preference.
142	    @discardableResult
143	    func expandByDefault() -> Bool {
144	        guard UserDefaults.standard.object(forKey: Self.collapsedKeyPrefix + id) == nil,
145	              !isExpanded
146	        else { return false }
147	        isExpanded = true
148	        content.isHidden = false
149	        header.isExpanded = true
150	        return true
151	    }

153	    func refresh() {
154	        refreshOptionControls(in: content)
155	        foldMarks()
156	    }

158	    /// The header's Clear (spec §11 CI-9): every key the section's rows
159	    /// write that the selected action holds, out of its end patch in ONE
160	    /// `set_action_end`.
161	    func clear() {
162	        let gutters = Self.gutters(in: content)
163	        guard let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap({ $0.binding }).first else { return }
164	        let keys = gutters.reduce(into: Set<String>()) { $0.formUnion($1.keyedWrites()) }
165	        binding.apply("Clear", binding.clearOps(keys))
166	    }

168	    /// The rows' gutters, in the order `refreshOptionControls(in:)` walks.
169	    private static func gutters(in view: NSView) -> [InspectorMarkGutter] {
170	        view.subviews.flatMap { subview -> [InspectorMarkGutter] in
171	            if let gutter = subview as? InspectorMarkGutter { return [gutter] }
172	            return gutters(in: subview)
173	        }
174	    }
175	
176	    /// `marks` from the gutters as they stand, then the two things drawn from
177	    /// it: the ⊘ note and the header. A section is EDITING the selected
178	    /// action when any of its rows animates; one that none does (Document,
179	    /// Shape, a ⊘-only section) keeps its Reset, since its edits go to the
180	    /// clip.
181	    private func foldMarks() {
182	        let gutters = Self.gutters(in: content)
183	        let writing = gutters.filter { !$0.writes.isEmpty }
184	        let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap { $0.binding }.first
185	        marks = SectionMarks(
186	            keyed: gutters.reduce(into: Set<String>()) { $0.formUnion($1.keyedWrites()) }.count,
187	            other: gutters.contains {
188	                if case .other = $0.mark { return true } else { return false }
189	            },
190	            allNotAnimatable: !writing.isEmpty
191	                && writing.allSatisfy { $0.mark == .notAnimatable },
192	            differs: differs?() ?? gutters.contains { $0.default?.differs() == true },
193	            editing: gutters.contains { $0.animates } ? binding?.selectedActionNumber : nil)
194	        inertNote?.refresh()
195	        header.refresh(summary: summary?(), marks: marks)
196	    }
197	}

199	/// The auto-open (spec §11 CI-8): the sections the selected action keys are
200	/// revealed on the sub-tab showing them, remembered for as long as that
201	/// action stays selected — so a rebuild under the same action re-reveals
202	/// them, a sub-tab first shown later adds its own, and a header click that
203	/// closes one drops it. One per `ClipPane`, applied at the end of every
204	/// `makeSections()`; it lives here because `ClipPane.swift` is at its cap.
205	final class KeyedReveal {
206	    private(set) var action: UInt32?
207	    private(set) var seen: Set<String> = []
208	    private(set) var ids: Set<String> = []
209	
210	    func apply(_ sections: [InspectorSection], action: UInt32?, subTab: String) {
211	        guard let action else {
212	            (self.action, seen, ids) = (nil, [], [])
213	            return
214	        }
215	        if action != self.action { (self.action, seen, ids) = (action, [], []) }
216	        if !seen.contains(subTab) {
217	            seen.insert(subTab)
218	            ids.formUnion(sections.filter { $0.marks.keyed > 0 }.map(\.id))
219	        }
220	        for section in sections {
221	            section.didToggle = { [weak self] in self?.ids.remove($0.id) }
222	            if ids.contains(section.id) { section.reveal() }
223	        }
224	    }
225	}

4	    // MARK: Writes
5	
6	    /// The part of a video patch that changes what the clip IS, and the part
7	    /// an action can animate. Either half may be nil; together they are the
8	    /// whole patch.
9	    ///
10	    /// **A list-valued key whose new LENGTH differs from the clip's own is
11	    /// the first kind, wherever the playhead sits.** `actions.rs`'s list rule
12	    /// interpolates an array PER INDEX only while the two lengths match, and
13	    /// otherwise holds the whole list at its start value and switches on the
14	    /// action's last tick. So a `filters` or `obscure` list of a different
15	    /// length written into an action's END patch is invisible for the entire
16	    /// span the user is looking at: the added region does not appear, and the
17	    /// section does not even grow a row, because `VideoPane`'s
18	    /// `structureSignature` counts the EVALUATED list. Worse, it does not
19	    /// survive: the next write of that list sends the whole array the pane
20	    /// can read — the base one, without the new entry — and replaces the end
21	    /// patch with it. Adding, removing and clearing therefore land on the
22	    /// BASE props even inside an action, where they are visible and keep.
23	    ///
24	    /// Dialling a value INSIDE an existing entry still goes to the action,
25	    /// which is what phase 3c's list rule exists for: a region's `amount`
26	    /// ramped from 0 to 1 is exactly that, and it works.
27	    ///
28	    /// The length is compared against `editedList` above — the action's own
29	    /// end list where there is one, the clip's base list otherwise — and never
30	    /// against the EVALUATED list the section reads, because that array is the
31	    /// one an end patch has to match to interpolate at all.
32	    ///
33	    /// **The sentence that used to stand here said "nothing the inspector does
34	    /// can put a different length into an end patch", and it was one action
35	    /// short of true.** With two actions on a clip and the first one's end
36	    /// patch changing the filter COUNT, the evaluated list at a playhead
37	    /// inside the SECOND action is longer than the base, so a comparison
38	    /// against the base classified an ordinary dial as structural and wrote
39	    /// the clip's base stack — changing every frame before the first action.
40	    /// With the pair above the section can only ever write the length it can
41	    /// see, so the guarantee holds; what it cannot promise is anything about a
42	    /// length a hand-written file or a `set_action_end` call put there.
43	    ///
44	    /// Do not fold this back into the single `set_action_end` it looks like.
45	    /// The two writes are the same shape from here and behave nothing alike
46	    /// three layers down, and every step of the failure is silent.
47	    ///
48	    /// Two residuals, both left deliberately and both smaller than what they
49	    /// replace:
50	    ///
51	    ///  - Changing an entry's DISCRIMINANT (a filter's `kind`, a region's
52	    ///    `kind` or `shape`) inside an action still writes the end patch,
53	    ///    because unlike a length change that IS a coherent animation —
54	    ///    `ENTRY_DISCRIMINANTS` in `actions.rs` holds the entry and switches
55	    ///    it at the end, which is what §5.4 says a discrete value does. It
56	    ///    reads back as unchanged until then, which is the inspector's
57	    ///    standing habit of showing the value AT THE PLAYHEAD while writing
58	    ///    the action's end, and not a property of lists.
59	    ///  - Adding or removing an entry while an action ALREADY animates that
60	    ///    list leaves the end patch at the old length, so that animation
61	    ///    degrades to a switch at the end until the end state is written
62	    ///    again. There is no way to say "drop this key" from here — a
63	    ///    `VideoPatch`'s list keys are single optionals, so nil is absent
64	    ///    rather than null — and a visible degradation is worth more than an
65	    ///    invisible append.
66	    private func structural(video patch: VideoPatch, for clip: ClipSnapshot)
67	        -> (base: VideoPatch?, animatable: VideoPatch?)
68	    {
69	        var base = VideoPatch()
70	        var animatable = patch
71	        if let filters = patch.filters,
72	            filters.count != editedList(clip, action: { $0.filters }, base: { $0.filters }).count
73	        {
74	            base.filters = filters
75	            animatable.filters = nil
76	        }
77	        if let obscure = patch.obscure,
78	            obscure.count != editedList(clip, action: { $0.obscure }, base: { $0.obscure }).count
79	        {
80	            base.obscure = obscure
81	            animatable.obscure = nil
82	        }
83	        // A curve is a list too (spec §11 GR-12, GR-32), but not this rule's:
84	        // every count animates (GR-34). The same count lerps per point, an
85	        // identity on either side is aligned to the other's x's
86	        // (`align_identity_curves`), and two curves of different counts blend
87	        // their values (`curve_blends`). So a curve write with an action
88	        // selected always goes to the END, a point added or deleted included,
89	        // and the curve is keyed and blends over the action.
90	        // Motion is not an animation target (the core refuses it in
91	        // `set_action_end`), so it ALWAYS lands on the base props.
92	        if patch.motion != nil {
93	            base.motion = patch.motion
94	            animatable.motion = nil
95	        }
96	        // A cutout's presence — a whole one or null — is the clip's (spec §11
97	        // CO-20, CO-30 (b)): an end refuses `subject`, `quality` and a null
98	        // cutout, so the Background section's checkbox and Reset land on the
99	        // base. Its sparse `cutoutPart` (Background, Edge, Feather) animates.
100	        if patch.cutout != nil {
101	            base.cutout = patch.cutout
102	            animatable.cutout = nil
103	        }
104	        // Hide while silent is not an animation target (spec §11 CO-92).
105	        if patch.hideSilent != nil {
106	            base.hideSilent = patch.hideSilent
107	            animatable.hideSilent = nil
108	        }
109	        // A cursor's `smoothing` and `hide_idle` are the clip's (spec §11 CU-30, CU-40): the
110	        // recipe reads them from the BASE, so an end carrying them would have no effect. Two
111	        // independent rules. (a) The clip's own keys go to the base; only the other six stay
112	        // in the end, an empty end part dropped. (b) An end key on a clip with no BASE cursor
113	        // also stores the defaults cursor on the base, merged with (a)'s keys, in the same
114	        // step — an end over no cursor switches at its end (CU-30), and with the defaults
115	        // stored Size and Ripple size animate. A whole cursor wins over `cursorPart` in
116	        // `VideoPatch.dictionary`, so (b)'s base carries (a)'s keys inside it.
117	        if let part = patch.cursorPart, !part.isEmpty {
118	            let own = part.clipsOwn
119	            let end = part.animatable
120	            if !own.isEmpty { animatable.cursorPart = end.isEmpty ? nil : end }
121	            if !end.isEmpty, clip.video?.cursor == nil {
122	                base.cursor = .some(
123	                    CursorProps(smoothing: own.smoothing ?? 0, hideIdle: own.hideIdle ?? nil))
124	            } else if !own.isEmpty {
125	                base.cursorPart = own
126	            }
127	        }
128	        return (base.isEmpty ? nil : base, animatable.isEmpty ? nil : animatable)
129	    }
130	
131	    /// The curve a write of `channel` replaces on `clip` (`editedList`'s
132	    /// rule): the selected action's end curve when the end names one, the
133	    /// clip's base curve otherwise (the identity when it has none).
134	    func editedCurve(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, _ channel: CurveChannel) -> [CurvePoint] {
135	        editedList(
136	            clip,
137	            action: { end -> [CurvePoint]? in
138	                guard case .some(.some(let list)) = end.curves?.entry(channel) else { return nil }
139	                return list
140	            },
141	            base: { $0.curves.points(channel) })
142	    }

145	    /// playhead is inside one, the base props otherwise — and the base props

147	    func ops(video patch: VideoPatch, for clip: ClipSnapshot) -> [ReelOp] {

154	    /// The selection's ops for a video patch. Clips outside an action share
155	    /// ONE `set_video` with several ids (§4.3); the ones inside get their own

164	    /// Spec §11 AU-88 (amending CI-3, AU-21, AU-37, AU-46, AU-50): with an
165	    /// action selected, pan, mono, the compressor, noise reduction, the
166	    /// limiter, isolation, the EQ, the hum notch, the channel pick, the gate,
167	    /// the leveller (AU-66) and the de-esser go to the action's END with

171	    /// NEST clip's mono stay the clip's (`AudioPatch.routedInsideAction`).

173	        -> (base: AudioPatch?, animatable: AudioPatch?)

181	            audioClips, patch, patch.isEmpty, base: { .setAudio(clips: $0, patch: $1) },

192	    /// Spec §11 G-34 (l): a graphic clip's props. Clips outside an action
193	    /// share ONE `set_graphic`, each value through G-15 (b)'s null rule
194	    /// (`patchProps`), so a base write is what it always was; a clip with an
195	    /// action selected gets one `set_action_end` naming `graphic.props.<key>`
196	    /// with the module's `schema`, each value as it is — a `null` in an end
197	    /// REMOVES (G-34 (j)) — except an asset's `null`, which is `""`, no image
198	    /// (`endValues`, G-42): an asset is now the end's. A prop that is not
199	    /// `animatable`, one its module marks `animate: false` (G-41), is the
200	    /// base's (an end refuses it, G-41 (b)), sent there by CI-3's mechanism.
201	    func ops(
202	        graphic values: [String: GraphicPropValue], entries: [GraphicSchemaEntry],
203	        clips: [ClipSnapshot], schema: [String: Any]?
204	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
205	        let held = Set(entries.filter { !$0.animatable }.map(\.key))
206	        return split(
207	            clips, values, values.isEmpty,
208	            base: {
209	                .setGraphicRaw(clips: $0, patch: ["props": GraphicSchemaRows.patchProps($1, entries: entries)], schema: schema)
210	            },
211	            action: { ActionPatch(graphic: ActionGraphicPatch(props: GraphicSchemaRows.endValues($0, entries: entries))) },
212	            schema: schema,
213	            structural: { values, _ in
214	                let base = values.filter { held.contains($0.key) }
215	                let animated = values.filter { !held.contains($0.key) }
216	                return (base.isEmpty ? nil : base, animated.isEmpty ? nil : animated)
217	            })
218	    }

220	    /// One row's write: `ops(graphic:entries:…)` for one entry.
221	    func ops(
222	        graphic value: GraphicPropValue, for entry: GraphicSchemaEntry,
223	        clips: [ClipSnapshot], schema: [String: Any]?
224	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
225	        ops(graphic: [entry.key: value], entries: [entry], clips: clips, schema: schema)
226	    }

228	    /// Shapes have no action form (§5.4's patch covers video, audio and text),
229	    /// so this is always one `set_shape` over every selected shape clip.
230	    func ops(shape patch: ShapePatch) -> [ReelOp] {
231	        let ids = shapeClips.map { $0.id }
232	        guard !patch.isEmpty, !ids.isEmpty else { return [] }
233	        return [.setShape(clips: ids, patch: patch)]

236	    /// The shared rule: clips outside an action share ONE op with several ids
237	    /// (§4.3's "one op with several clip ids"); each clip the playhead is
238	    /// inside an action of gets its own `set_action_end` instead — less the
239	    /// part `structural` pulls back onto its base props, which is a change to
240	    /// the clip and not to how it animates.
241	    ///
242	    /// Audio and text pass no `structural`, and the default says why they
243	    /// need none: `VideoPatch` is the only patch with an array-valued key, so
244	    /// video is the only one whose write can change a LENGTH. `schema` goes with
245	    /// every `set_action_end`; only a graphic end needs one (G-34 (c)).
246	    private func split<Patch>(
247	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], _ patch: Patch, _ isEmpty: Bool,
248	        base: ([UInt32], Patch) -> ReelOp,
249	        action end: (Patch) -> ActionPatch, schema: [String: Any]? = nil,
250	        structural: (Patch, ClipSnapshot) -> (base: Patch?, animatable: Patch?) = {
251	            whole, _ in (base: nil, animatable: whole)
252	        }
253	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
254	        guard !isEmpty, !clips.isEmpty else { return [] }
255	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
256	        var ids: [UInt32] = []
257	        for clip in clips {
258	            guard let inside = action(clip) else {
259	                ids.append(clip.id)
260	                continue
261	            }
262	            let parts = structural(patch, clip)
263	            if let onClip = parts.base { ops.append(base([clip.id], onClip)) }
264	            if let animated = parts.animatable {
265	                ops.append(
266	                    .setActionEnd(clip: clip.id, action: inside.id, patch: end(animated), schema: schema))
267	            }
268	        }
269	        if !ids.isEmpty { ops.insert(base(ids, patch), at: 0) }
270	        return ops
271	    }

331	/// thirds, and every other visible layer's edges and centres.

334	/// has no idea where anything sits on screen — but the nearest-within-
335	/// threshold *pick* is `ReelSnap.resolve` (i.e. `rc_snap_resolve`), so the
336	/// canvas and the timeline snap by the same rule. That function speaks in
337	/// `Ticks`, so canvas coordinates are rounded to whole pixels on the way in;
338	/// a snap is always to a pixel, which is what the guides promise anyway.
339	struct CanvasSnapper {
340	    /// Grab radius in VIEW points, converted to canvas pixels per zoom.
341	    static let threshold: CGFloat = 8
342	
343	    let xs: [Ticks]
344	    let ys: [Ticks]
345	    /// The radius in canvas pixels at the current zoom.
346	    let threshold: Ticks
347	    /// Folds together the N toggle and the ⌘ suppression, so no session ever
348	    /// looks at modifier flags itself.
349	    let enabled: Bool
350	
351	    /// What a proposed rectangle has to move by to sit on a candidate, plus
352	    /// the guide lines to draw (canvas coordinates, nil when nothing snapped).
353	    struct Result {
354	        var offset = CGVector.zero
355	        var guideX: CGFloat?
356	        var guideY: CGFloat?
357	    }
358	
359	    /// Tries the rectangle's leading edge, centre and trailing edge on each
360	    /// axis and takes the smallest correction of the three.
361	    func resolve(rect: CGRect) -> Result {
362	        var result = Result()
363	        guard enabled else { return result }
364	        if let hit = best(of: [rect.minX, rect.midX, rect.maxX], in: xs) {
365	            result.offset.dx = hit.delta
366	            result.guideX = hit.guide
367	        }
368	        if let hit = best(of: [rect.minY, rect.midY, rect.maxY], in: ys) {
369	            result.offset.dy = hit.delta
370	            result.guideY = hit.guide
371	        }
372	        return result
373	    }
374	
375	    private func best(
376	        of anchors: [CGFloat], in candidates: [Ticks]
377	    ) -> (delta: CGFloat, guide: CGFloat)? {
378	        var winner: (delta: CGFloat, guide: CGFloat)?
379	        for anchor in anchors {
380	            let (resolved, snapped) = ReelSnap.resolve(
381	                candidates, CanvasSnapper.tick(anchor), threshold: threshold)
382	            guard snapped else { continue }
383	            let delta = CGFloat(resolved) - anchor
384	            if let current = winner, abs(current.delta) <= abs(delta) { continue }
385	            winner = (delta, CGFloat(resolved))
386	        }
387	        return winner
388	    }
389	
390	    /// A canvas coordinate as a whole pixel, clamped well inside `Int64` so a
391	    /// runaway drag cannot trap the conversion.
392	    static func tick(_ value: CGFloat) -> Ticks {
393	        guard value.isFinite else { return 0 }
394	        return Ticks(min(max(value.rounded(), -1e9), 1e9))
395	    }
396	
397	    /// Canvas landmarks plus the other layers'. `excluding` is the clips the
398	    /// gesture is moving — a drag must not snap to itself.
399	    static func candidates(
400	        boxes: [CanvasLayerBox], excluding: Set<UInt32>, canvas: CanvasSnapshot
401	    ) -> (xs: [Ticks], ys: [Ticks]) {
402	        let width = CGFloat(canvas.width)
403	        let height = CGFloat(canvas.height)
404	        var xs: Set<Ticks> = [
405	            tick(0), tick(width / 3), tick(width / 2), tick(width * 2 / 3), tick(width),
406	        ]
407	        var ys: Set<Ticks> = [
408	            tick(0), tick(height / 3), tick(height / 2), tick(height * 2 / 3), tick(height),
409	        ]
410	        for box in boxes where !excluding.contains(box.id) {
411	            let bounds = box.bounds
412	            xs.formUnion([tick(bounds.minX), tick(bounds.midX), tick(bounds.maxX)])
413	            ys.formUnion([tick(bounds.minY), tick(bounds.midY), tick(bounds.maxY)])
414	        }
415	        return (xs.sorted(), ys.sorted())
416	    }
417	}

419	/// Trims a canvas coordinate to three decimals before it goes into an op.
420	/// Snapping produces whole or half pixels; this only keeps float noise out of
421	/// the project JSON, where it would make two identical edits compare unequal.
422	func canvasRound(_ value: Double) -> Double {
423	    guard value.isFinite else { return 0 }
424	    return (value * 1000).rounded() / 1000
425	}
426	
427	/// A colour as `video.chroma.key`: exactly three components, clamped to 0…1.
428	///
429	/// That key is the ONE colour in the schema the model spells without an alpha
430	/// (`[f64; 3]` in `model.rs`, and `props_check.rs` bounds each channel), so a
431	/// four-component `RGBA` — which is what a colour well hands back, and what
432	/// the comparison in `changedRGBA` needs — has to be cut back to three before
433	/// it can reach `set_video`. A longer array is not a warning there: serde
434	/// answers `invalid length 4, expected an array of length 3` and the whole
435	/// edit fails.
436	func chromaKeyComponents(_ color: RGBA) -> [Double] {
437	    (0..<3).map { index in
438	        let value = index < color.count ? color[index] : 0
439	        return canvasRound(min(max(value, 0), 1))
440	    }
441	}

445	/// Dragging inside the box to move the selection (spec §4.2). Every selected
446	/// clip moves by the same canvas-space delta; the anchor clip's rectangle is
447	/// what snapping tests, so the whole selection clicks into place together.
448	///
449	/// The op writes the target's props plus the delta (the base, or the selected
450	/// action's end state — CI-13), never the evaluated position at the playhead.
451	struct CanvasMoveSession {
452	    /// The target's `(x, y)` per clip, captured at mouse-down.
453	    let bases: [UInt32: CGPoint]
454	    let anchor: UInt32
455	    /// The anchor's rotated bounds at mouse-down.
456	    let anchorBounds: CGRect
457	    /// Pointer position at mouse-down, canvas space.
458	    let grab: CGPoint
459	
460	    var delta = CGVector.zero
461	    var guideX: CGFloat?
462	    var guideY: CGFloat?
463	    /// False until the pointer actually leaves the press point — a click that
464	    /// only selects must not register an undo step.
465	    var didMove = false
466	
467	    /// One op per clip, routed by `target`: each keeps its own position, so
468	    /// a multi-clip move cannot collapse the selection onto one point.
469	    func ops(to target: CanvasEditTarget) -> [ReelOp] {
470	        bases.keys.sorted().compactMap { id in
471	            guard let base = bases[id] else { return nil }
472	            return target.op(
473	                video: VideoPatch(
474	                    x: canvasRound(base.x + delta.dx), y: canvasRound(base.y + delta.dy)),
475	                clip: id)
476	        }
477	    }
478	
479	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint, snapper: CanvasSnapper) {
480	        var raw = CGVector(dx: point.x - grab.x, dy: point.y - grab.y)
481	        let proposed = anchorBounds.offsetBy(dx: raw.dx, dy: raw.dy)
482	        let result = snapper.resolve(rect: proposed)
483	        raw.dx += result.offset.dx
484	        raw.dy += result.offset.dy
485	        delta = raw
486	        guideX = result.guideX
487	        guideY = result.guideY
488	        didMove = true
489	    }
490	}

494	/// What a scale drag is allowed to change, which depends on what the model
495	/// stores for that clip (§5.2).
496	///
497	/// **The pitfall:** a clip has ONE uniform `scale` — there is no per-axis
498	/// scale for pixels. So "edges scale one axis" and "⇧ frees the aspect" can
499	/// only be honoured where the model owns a second number: a shape's
500	/// `width`/`height`, or a text clip's wrap `width`. Everywhere else a drag
501	/// stays uniform rather than pretending otherwise.
502	enum CanvasScaleTarget: Equatable {
503	    /// Media, stills, images, nests — `video.scale` only.
504	    case uniform
505	    /// A shape's box, in model units.
506	    case box(CGSize)
507	    /// A text clip's wrap width (nil = auto-sized); the measured width at
508	    /// mouse-down stands in for it.
509	    case textWidth(Double)
510	}
511	
512	/// One clip resized by one of the eight handles (spec §4.2). ⌥ scales about
513	/// the centre; without it the opposite handle is pinned, which means the
514	/// clip's position moves too — hence the `x`/`y` in the patch.
515	struct CanvasScaleSession {
516	    let clip: UInt32
517	    let handle: CanvasHandle
518	    let target: CanvasScaleTarget
519	    /// The target's video props at mouse-down (`CanvasEditTarget.start`).
520	    let base: VideoProps
521	    /// The uncropped rectangle at mouse-down, un-rotated, canvas space. Its
522	    /// centre IS the rotation anchor, which is what makes the position
523	    /// correction below a plain rotation of the centre's displacement.
524	    let startRect: CGRect
525	    let rotation: Double
526	
527	    var scale: Double
528	    var boxSize: CGSize
529	    var textWidth: Double
530	    /// True once a `.textWidth` drag has actually taken the width path. The
531	    /// other six handles of a text clip fall back to a uniform scale, and
532	    /// `ops` must then emit `set_video` rather than `set_text`.
533	    var widthOnly = false
534	    /// Change in the clip's `(x, y)`, canvas space.
535	    var offset = CGVector.zero

163	        guard let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap({ $0.binding }).first else { return }

170	        view.subviews.flatMap { subview -> [InspectorMarkGutter] in
171	            if let gutter = subview as? InspectorMarkGutter { return [gutter] }

177	    /// it: the ⊘ note and the header. A section is EDITING the selected
178	    /// action when any of its rows animates; one that none does (Document,
179	    /// Shape, a ⊘-only section) keeps its Reset, since its edits go to the
180	    /// clip.
181	    private func foldMarks() {
182	        let gutters = Self.gutters(in: content)
183	        let writing = gutters.filter { !$0.writes.isEmpty }
184	        let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap { $0.binding }.first
185	        marks = SectionMarks(
186	            keyed: gutters.reduce(into: Set<String>()) { $0.formUnion($1.keyedWrites()) }.count,
187	            other: gutters.contains {
188	                if case .other = $0.mark { return true } else { return false }
189	            },
190	            allNotAnimatable: !writing.isEmpty
191	                && writing.allSatisfy { $0.mark == .notAnimatable },
192	            differs: differs?() ?? gutters.contains { $0.default?.differs() == true },
193	            editing: gutters.contains { $0.animates } ? binding?.selectedActionNumber : nil)
194	        inertNote?.refresh()
195	        header.refresh(summary: summary?(), marks: marks)

199	/// The auto-open (spec §11 CI-8): the sections the selected action keys are
200	/// revealed on the sub-tab showing them, remembered for as long as that
201	/// action stays selected — so a rebuild under the same action re-reveals
202	/// them, a sub-tab first shown later adds its own, and a header click that
203	/// closes one drops it. One per `ClipPane`, applied at the end of every
204	/// `makeSections()`; it lives here because `ClipPane.swift` is at its cap.
205	final class KeyedReveal {
206	    private(set) var action: UInt32?
207	    private(set) var seen: Set<String> = []
208	    private(set) var ids: Set<String> = []
209	
210	    func apply(_ sections: [InspectorSection], action: UInt32?, subTab: String) {
211	        guard let action else {
212	            (self.action, seen, ids) = (nil, [], [])
213	            return
214	        }
215	        if action != self.action { (self.action, seen, ids) = (action, [], []) }
216	        if !seen.contains(subTab) {
217	            seen.insert(subTab)
218	            ids.formUnion(sections.filter { $0.marks.keyed > 0 }.map(\.id))
219	        }
220	        for section in sections {
221	            section.didToggle = { [weak self] in self?.ids.remove($0.id) }
222	            if ids.contains(section.id) { section.reveal() }
223	        }
224	    }
225	}

3	extension InspectorBinding {
4	    // MARK: Writes
5	
6	    /// The part of a video patch that changes what the clip IS, and the part
7	    /// an action can animate. Either half may be nil; together they are the
8	    /// whole patch.
9	    ///
10	    /// **A list-valued key whose new LENGTH differs from the clip's own is
11	    /// the first kind, wherever the playhead sits.** `actions.rs`'s list rule
12	    /// interpolates an array PER INDEX only while the two lengths match, and
13	    /// otherwise holds the whole list at its start value and switches on the
14	    /// action's last tick. So a `filters` or `obscure` list of a different
15	    /// length written into an action's END patch is invisible for the entire
16	    /// span the user is looking at: the added region does not appear, and the
17	    /// section does not even grow a row, because `VideoPane`'s
18	    /// `structureSignature` counts the EVALUATED list. Worse, it does not
19	    /// survive: the next write of that list sends the whole array the pane
20	    /// can read — the base one, without the new entry — and replaces the end
21	    /// patch with it. Adding, removing and clearing therefore land on the
22	    /// BASE props even inside an action, where they are visible and keep.
23	    ///
24	    /// Dialling a value INSIDE an existing entry still goes to the action,
25	    /// which is what phase 3c's list rule exists for: a region's `amount`
26	    /// ramped from 0 to 1 is exactly that, and it works.
27	    ///
28	    /// The length is compared against `editedList` above — the action's own
29	    /// end list where there is one, the clip's base list otherwise — and never
30	    /// against the EVALUATED list the section reads, because that array is the
31	    /// one an end patch has to match to interpolate at all.
32	    ///
33	    /// **The sentence that used to stand here said "nothing the inspector does
34	    /// can put a different length into an end patch", and it was one action
35	    /// short of true.** With two actions on a clip and the first one's end
36	    /// patch changing the filter COUNT, the evaluated list at a playhead
37	    /// inside the SECOND action is longer than the base, so a comparison
38	    /// against the base classified an ordinary dial as structural and wrote
39	    /// the clip's base stack — changing every frame before the first action.
40	    /// With the pair above the section can only ever write the length it can
41	    /// see, so the guarantee holds; what it cannot promise is anything about a
42	    /// length a hand-written file or a `set_action_end` call put there.
43	    ///
44	    /// Do not fold this back into the single `set_action_end` it looks like.
45	    /// The two writes are the same shape from here and behave nothing alike
46	    /// three layers down, and every step of the failure is silent.
47	    ///
48	    /// Two residuals, both left deliberately and both smaller than what they
49	    /// replace:
50	    ///
51	    ///  - Changing an entry's DISCRIMINANT (a filter's `kind`, a region's
52	    ///    `kind` or `shape`) inside an action still writes the end patch,
53	    ///    because unlike a length change that IS a coherent animation —
54	    ///    `ENTRY_DISCRIMINANTS` in `actions.rs` holds the entry and switches
55	    ///    it at the end, which is what §5.4 says a discrete value does. It
56	    ///    reads back as unchanged until then, which is the inspector's
57	    ///    standing habit of showing the value AT THE PLAYHEAD while writing
58	    ///    the action's end, and not a property of lists.
59	    ///  - Adding or removing an entry while an action ALREADY animates that
60	    ///    list leaves the end patch at the old length, so that animation
61	    ///    degrades to a switch at the end until the end state is written
62	    ///    again. There is no way to say "drop this key" from here — a
63	    ///    `VideoPatch`'s list keys are single optionals, so nil is absent
64	    ///    rather than null — and a visible degradation is worth more than an
65	    ///    invisible append.
66	    private func structural(video patch: VideoPatch, for clip: ClipSnapshot)
67	        -> (base: VideoPatch?, animatable: VideoPatch?)
68	    {
69	        var base = VideoPatch()
70	        var animatable = patch
71	        if let filters = patch.filters,
72	            filters.count != editedList(clip, action: { $0.filters }, base: { $0.filters }).count
73	        {
74	            base.filters = filters
75	            animatable.filters = nil
76	        }
77	        if let obscure = patch.obscure,
78	            obscure.count != editedList(clip, action: { $0.obscure }, base: { $0.obscure }).count
79	        {
80	            base.obscure = obscure
81	            animatable.obscure = nil
82	        }
83	        // A curve is a list too (spec §11 GR-12, GR-32), but not this rule's:
84	        // every count animates (GR-34). The same count lerps per point, an
85	        // identity on either side is aligned to the other's x's
86	        // (`align_identity_curves`), and two curves of different counts blend
87	        // their values (`curve_blends`). So a curve write with an action
88	        // selected always goes to the END, a point added or deleted included,
89	        // and the curve is keyed and blends over the action.
90	        // Motion is not an animation target (the core refuses it in
91	        // `set_action_end`), so it ALWAYS lands on the base props.
92	        if patch.motion != nil {
93	            base.motion = patch.motion
94	            animatable.motion = nil
95	        }
96	        // A cutout's presence — a whole one or null — is the clip's (spec §11
97	        // CO-20, CO-30 (b)): an end refuses `subject`, `quality` and a null
98	        // cutout, so the Background section's checkbox and Reset land on the
99	        // base. Its sparse `cutoutPart` (Background, Edge, Feather) animates.
100	        if patch.cutout != nil {
101	            base.cutout = patch.cutout
102	            animatable.cutout = nil
103	        }
104	        // Hide while silent is not an animation target (spec §11 CO-92).
105	        if patch.hideSilent != nil {
106	            base.hideSilent = patch.hideSilent
107	            animatable.hideSilent = nil
108	        }
109	        // A cursor's `smoothing` and `hide_idle` are the clip's (spec §11 CU-30, CU-40): the
110	        // recipe reads them from the BASE, so an end carrying them would have no effect. Two
111	        // independent rules. (a) The clip's own keys go to the base; only the other six stay
112	        // in the end, an empty end part dropped. (b) An end key on a clip with no BASE cursor
113	        // also stores the defaults cursor on the base, merged with (a)'s keys, in the same
114	        // step — an end over no cursor switches at its end (CU-30), and with the defaults
115	        // stored Size and Ripple size animate. A whole cursor wins over `cursorPart` in
116	        // `VideoPatch.dictionary`, so (b)'s base carries (a)'s keys inside it.
117	        if let part = patch.cursorPart, !part.isEmpty {
118	            let own = part.clipsOwn
119	            let end = part.animatable
120	            if !own.isEmpty { animatable.cursorPart = end.isEmpty ? nil : end }
121	            if !end.isEmpty, clip.video?.cursor == nil {
122	                base.cursor = .some(
123	                    CursorProps(smoothing: own.smoothing ?? 0, hideIdle: own.hideIdle ?? nil))
124	            } else if !own.isEmpty {
125	                base.cursorPart = own
126	            }
127	        }
128	        return (base.isEmpty ? nil : base, animatable.isEmpty ? nil : animatable)
129	    }

192	    /// Spec §11 G-34 (l): a graphic clip's props. Clips outside an action
193	    /// share ONE `set_graphic`, each value through G-15 (b)'s null rule
194	    /// (`patchProps`), so a base write is what it always was; a clip with an

198	    /// (`endValues`, G-42): an asset is now the end's. A prop that is not
199	    /// `animatable`, one its module marks `animate: false` (G-41), is the
200	    /// base's (an end refuses it, G-41 (b)), sent there by CI-3's mechanism.
201	    func ops(
202	        graphic values: [String: GraphicPropValue], entries: [GraphicSchemaEntry],
203	        clips: [ClipSnapshot], schema: [String: Any]?
204	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
205	        let held = Set(entries.filter { !$0.animatable }.map(\.key))
206	        return split(
207	            clips, values, values.isEmpty,
208	            base: {
209	                .setGraphicRaw(clips: $0, patch: ["props": GraphicSchemaRows.patchProps($1, entries: entries)], schema: schema)
210	            },
211	            action: { ActionPatch(graphic: ActionGraphicPatch(props: GraphicSchemaRows.endValues($0, entries: entries))) },
212	            schema: schema,
213	            structural: { values, _ in
214	                let base = values.filter { held.contains($0.key) }
215	                let animated = values.filter { !held.contains($0.key) }
216	                return (base.isEmpty ? nil : base, animated.isEmpty ? nil : animated)

237	    /// (§4.3's "one op with several clip ids"); each clip the playhead is
238	    /// inside an action of gets its own `set_action_end` instead — less the
239	    /// part `structural` pulls back onto its base props, which is a change to
240	    /// the clip and not to how it animates.
241	    ///
242	    /// Audio and text pass no `structural`, and the default says why they
243	    /// need none: `VideoPatch` is the only patch with an array-valued key, so
244	    /// video is the only one whose write can change a LENGTH. `schema` goes with
245	    /// every `set_action_end`; only a graphic end needs one (G-34 (c)).
246	    private func split<Patch>(
247	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], _ patch: Patch, _ isEmpty: Bool,
248	        base: ([UInt32], Patch) -> ReelOp,
249	        action end: (Patch) -> ActionPatch, schema: [String: Any]? = nil,
250	        structural: (Patch, ClipSnapshot) -> (base: Patch?, animatable: Patch?) = {
251	            whole, _ in (base: nil, animatable: whole)
252	        }
253	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
254	        guard !isEmpty, !clips.isEmpty else { return [] }
255	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
256	        var ids: [UInt32] = []
257	        for clip in clips {
258	            guard let inside = action(clip) else {
259	                ids.append(clip.id)
260	                continue
261	            }
262	            let parts = structural(patch, clip)
263	            if let onClip = parts.base { ops.append(base([clip.id], onClip)) }
264	            if let animated = parts.animatable {
265	                ops.append(
266	                    .setActionEnd(clip: clip.id, action: inside.id, patch: end(animated), schema: schema))
267	            }
268	        }
269	        if !ids.isEmpty { ops.insert(base(ids, patch), at: 0) }
270	        return ops
271	    }
