What you're cutting away shows as a dim ghost, inside a dashed outline of the uncropped frame.

39	In crop mode the eight square handles become crop edges and the rotation grip goes away. A corner handle moves two edges, and a side handle moves one.
40	
41	What you're cutting away shows as a dim ghost, inside a dashed outline of the uncropped frame.
42	
43	- A drag changes the crop and nothing else. The clip's position stays put, and the picture doesn't shift.
44	- A crop drag doesn't snap.
45	- At least one source pixel always remains in each direction, however far you drag.
46	- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during a drag to cancel it. The crop goes back to where it was, with no undo step.
47	- Each finished drag is one undo step.
48	
49	Dragging inside the box still moves the clip, as it does outside crop mode. With several clips selected, the handles belong to the front-most one and crop only that clip.
50	
51	## Leaving crop mode
52	
53	Your crop stays when you leave. Any of these leaves crop mode:
54	
55	| Do this | Good to know |
56	| --- | --- |
57	| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. |
58	| Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. During a drag, the first <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels the drag and the next one leaves the mode. |
59	| Press <kbd>C</kbd> or choose **Crop on Canvas** | Works wherever the focus is, except while you're typing in a field. |
60	| Click empty canvas | This also clears the selection, unless you hold <kbd>⇧</kbd>. |
61	| Click a different clip on the canvas | That clip becomes the selection. |
62	
63	The canvas has focus once you've clicked or dragged on it. If you pressed <kbd>C</kbd> and haven't touched the canvas yet, press <kbd>C</kbd> again to leave.
64	
65	Crop mode also ends if nothing selected is left on the canvas, for example when you clear the selection in the timeline.
66	
67	## The Crop section
68	
69	The **Crop** section on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) has the same four edges as fields, for when you want an exact number. It shows only for video, image and still clips.
70	
71	| Field | What it does | Default | Range |
72	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
73	| **Left** | Source pixels cut from the left edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
74	| **Top** | Source pixels cut from the top edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
75	| **Right** | Source pixels cut from the right edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
76	| **Bottom** | Source pixels cut from the bottom edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
77	
78	These are typed fields, with no slider. **Crop on Canvas** under them goes in and out of crop mode.
79	
80	Closed, the section's summary reads `none`, or the four amounts in field order, such as `100·0·100·0`. **Reset** appears in the section's header while there's a crop, and takes all four edges back to 0.
81	
82	Left and Right together must stay under the picture's width, and Top and Bottom under its height. If a number would use up the whole picture, Frame Job shows an error and keeps the crop you had.
83	
84	:::caution
85	With several clips selected, editing one field gives every clip all four of the first clip's amounts, not only the edge you changed. Crop clips of different sizes one at a time.
86	:::
87	
88	## How a crop works
89	
90	A crop removes edges in place. The picture you keep stays exactly where it was on the canvas, so cropping the left edge opens a gap on the left rather than sliding the picture over.
91	
92	The amounts are in the source's own pixels, not canvas pixels, so they stay correct when you scale the clip later. Cutting 100 px from a clip at 50 % takes 50 canvas pixels off it, and the same 100 px at 200 % takes 200.
93	
94	Position, scale and rotation go on measuring from the centre of the uncropped picture. A crop doesn't recentre what's left, so move the clip if you want that.
95	
96	- [Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas](/canvas/transform/#fit-and-fill) measure the uncropped picture too.
97	- [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/) and the [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follow the cropped edge.
98	- [Reset in Transform](/canvas/transform/#reset) leaves the crop alone.
99	
100	## Animate a crop
101	
102	A crop can change over time. With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected on a single clip, a crop handle or a field sets the crop at the action's end, and the edges move there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
103	
104	While you're editing an action, the section's **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes the crop out of that action.
105	
106	## Good to know
107	
108	- Crop mode has no menu item. It's <kbd>C</kbd>, a double-click, or the **Crop on Canvas** button.
109	- <kbd>C</kbd> also opens crop mode on a text, shape, graphic or nest clip, and a double-click does on all of those except text. They have no Crop section, so there are no fields and no **Reset**. To take that crop off, undo or drag the handles back.
110	- A clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) shows no crop handles.

35	It rounds the [cropped](/canvas/crop/) picture, so the curve follows the crop rather than the original frame. A [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follows the rounded shape.
36	
37	A radius can't be more than half the picture's shorter side, and anything above that draws as that half. So a big enough radius turns a wide picture into a pill and a square picture into a circle.
38

39	## Scale
40	
41	At 100 % a video or picture draws at its native pixels, one source pixel to one canvas pixel, so a 1920 × 1080 clip on a 3840 × 2160 canvas covers a quarter of it. The field takes one decimal place.
42	
43	Scale pivots on the centre of the uncropped picture. It works on every clip that draws, text, shapes and graphics included.
44	
45	## Position
46	
47	Position places the clip's centre in canvas pixels, measured from the centre of the canvas. At 0, 0 the clip sits in the middle. **Position X** runs right and **Position Y** runs down, so negative values go left and up.
48	
49	Both are typed fields in whole pixels, with no slider. On a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip they still measure the centre of the uncropped picture.
50	
51	## Rotation
52	
53	Rotation turns the clip about its centre, and a positive angle turns it clockwise on screen. The field takes one decimal place.
54	
55	## Opacity
56	
57	Opacity sets how see-through the clip is: at 100 % it's solid, and at 0 % it's fully transparent.
58	
59	## Fit and fill
60	
61	Both buttons scale each selected clip and centre it, setting its position to 0, 0.
62	
63	- **Fit to Canvas** makes the whole picture fit inside the canvas, so you may see the background at two edges.
64	- **Fill Canvas** makes the picture cover the whole canvas, so its edges may run off two sides.
65	
66	Each clip gets its own scale from its own size, and all of them together are one undo step. A shape uses its box, a graphic its size and a nest its own canvas.
67	
68	Good to know:
69	
70	- Text clips are skipped, because their size comes from the words. So is any clip with no known size. If that leaves nothing to scale, Frame Job beeps.
71	- Both buttons measure the uncropped picture, so a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip can leave a gap after **Fill Canvas**.
72	- Rotation stays as it is and isn't counted, so a rotated clip may not fit or fill the way it would upright.
73	- A scale past the 1 to 1000 % range isn't applied, so a very small picture on a large canvas can get an error from **Fill Canvas** instead.
74	
75	## Reset
76	
77	**Reset** in the section's header puts position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur back to their defaults in one step. It shows only while the section differs from its default.
78	
79	It leaves the [crop](/canvas/crop/) alone, which has its own **Reset**. To put back a single row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
80	
81	## Animate these values
82	
83	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur set the action's end state, and the clip ramps there along the action's curve. Blend switches at the action's end instead. **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes the section out of the action.
84	
85	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
86	
87	## No stretching
88	
89	Scale is uniform for pictures. A video, image, graphic or nest always keeps its proportions, and there's no separate width and height.
90	
91	Only two kinds of clip can change on one axis: a shape, through its box's width and height, and text, through its wrap width. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) and [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).
92	
93	## Related

71	**Pick a colour.** A colour swatch opens the macOS Colors panel, with opacity.
72	
73	**Edit inside an action.** With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, the rows read and write the action's end state, and the sections it animates open by themselves. **Reset** gives way to **Clear**, which takes that section out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
74	
75	[Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers typing, sliders and the quick picks in a field's menu.

| Esc during any drag | Cancel the drag and put the clip back where it was, with no undo step |

How a scale drag behaves depends on the clip:

- **Video, image, still, graphic and nest clips** have one uniform scale. Every
  handle scales the whole picture and keeps its aspect ratio.
- **Shape clips** change their box size instead. A corner handle keeps the
  aspect ratio and ⇧ frees it. An edge handle changes only the width or only
  the height.
- **Text clips**: the left and right edge handles set the text box's wrap
  width, which makes the box fixed-width. The corners and the top and bottom

With an action selected on the clip's action lane, a move, scale, rotate or
crop drag, or an arrow-key nudge, edits that action's end state, just as the
inspector's fields do. The box on screen still shows the frame at the
playhead. There are two exceptions: a drag on a multi-clip selection, and a
shape's box resize, both edit the clip itself. See
[Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

## Crop

Press **C**, or double-click a clip that is not text, to enter crop mode for
the selected clip. The eight handles become crop edges, and the part being
cut away is shown as a dim ghost inside the uncropped frame. Press **Esc** or
**Return**, or click empty canvas, to leave crop mode.

A crop removes edges in place: the picture never shifts as you crop. Crop
amounts are in the source's own pixels, so they stay correct when you scale
the clip later. The core keeps at least one source pixel in each direction.

The Picture tab's **Crop** section has the same four insets as fields, plus a
**Crop on Canvas** button that enters crop mode. Crop appears only for clips
- **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip** follow where they apply.

An adjustment clip has no Picture tab, because it has no picture of its own
(see [Color grading](color-grading.md)).

Picture's sections, in order:

| Section | Shown for |
|---|---|
| Transform | every clip that draws |
| Behind Subject | every clip that draws but an adjustment or nest clip, at the top level |
| Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key | video, image and still clips |
| Background | clips of a video file, freeze frames of one, and image clips |
| Cursor | clips of a movie whose cursor file the picture doesn't already show ([The cursor](screen-recording.md#the-cursor)) |
| Shadow, Filters, Reflection, Spotlight, Obscure | every clip that draws, text and shapes included |

Each section folds open and shut and shows a one-line summary while closed.
Transform starts open. **Reset** appears only while a section differs from its
default. With several clips selected, a field shows the first clip's value and
a mixed badge when the others differ. An edit applies to every selected clip.
Colour swatches open the macOS Colors panel, with opacity.

*Agents:* `set_video` (merges a patch into each clip's video properties: `x`,
`y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `blend`, `crop`, `corner_radius`,
`shadow`, `chroma`, `filters`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `obscure`).

### Transform

| Row | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Scale | 1–1000 % (quick values 25–400) | 100 % |
| Position X / Y | −20000 to 20000 canvas px, measured from the canvas centre, X right and Y down | 0, 0 |
| Rotation | −180° to 180° | 0° |
| Opacity | 0–100 % | 100 % |
| Blend | the eight blend modes below | Normal |
| Motion Blur | 0–100 % of a frame (quick values 0, 25, 50, 100); greyed on a nest or adjustment clip ([Motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur)) | 0 % |

Two buttons sit under the rows:

- **Fit to Canvas** scales each clip so its whole picture fits, and centres it.
- **Fill Canvas** scales each clip until it covers the whole canvas, and
  centres it.

non-black canvas background on the Document tab. The Blend popup's tooltip
gives the same explanation.

Limits:

- A cross dissolve draws as Normal for as long as the clips overlap.
- The Blend popup is greyed on a nest clip, because a nest has no pixels of its
  own to blend. Un-nest it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside.
- Blend is an ordinary property, so an action can change it. Like any
  on/off-style value, the change happens at the action's end.

### Corner Radius

Radius: 0–500 px in source pixels (quick values 0–64). It rounds the cropped
picture's corners. Default 0.

All five pages are checked: canvas/crop, canvas/picture-tab, canvas/transform, canvas/blend-modes and canvas/corner-radius. canvas/blend-modes needed no change. After the edits, check-pages.mjs reported 5 pages, 0 problems and docs_site_proof.py --pages reported 0 problems. No heading changed, so the anchors file was not edited. Nothing documented is dev-only. The 05-clip-picture screen matches its alt text on both pages that use it. Two things need someone else:

1. docs/site/src/data/features.json was left alone because it is shared. Its crop-leave summary still says \"Return, keypad Enter, Esc, C\" and its crop-handles summary still says \"dim ghost\". Both now disagree with the page.

2. Two possible app defects, found by reading the code only, not run. The pages describe what the code does.
- app/Sources/PreviewCanvasView.swift:469 compares primaryBox to the clicked clip after selectClip has already changed the selection, so the leave-on-click branch never fires for an unselected clip. It looks intended to leave crop mode.
- app/Sources/PreviewCanvasView.swift:663 rejects any flag but Shift, while app/Sources/EditorWindow.swift:106 allows .numericPad and .function for the same keys. If those flags are set as that code implies, keypad Enter never reaches its arm. Arrow keys normally carry those flags too, so the canvas nudge at :683-687 may also be unreachable. Whoever checks canvas/move-scale-rotate should weigh that claim.
